capture, sha256

resolution IS. Each one names the source change, and several carry a measurement

What the loop measured, rather than asserted:
round 1  6/6 reviewers led with the same P1 — the product's entire call to
action rendered as the weakest control on the page. The primary
button measured 1.04:1 before and 6.29:1 after.
round 2  that P1 is gone from all six. New: the section-heading level
collides with the hero identifier; one grey does four jobs.
round 3  L2 measures the rhythm and reports 'one scale, correct proximity',
and that 'the classic label/value misalignment this view is warned
about did not happen'. L1 calls the type scale 'sound'.
round 4  the last foundations P1 clears. Remaining findings are P2/P3.
round 5  RECORDED BELOW. ZERO P1s carry a rubric criterion — every P1 is a
presence failure. L3 independently measured every text-on-surface

Every round-5 P1 is a PRESENCE failure — age, a copy affordance, the value /
nonce / type rows, the receipt payload, the 'supply an ABI' action. That is
content nobody has built. All fifteen are recorded verbatim, none is
resolved, and the FULL gate holds every one against this page (G1 and G3 both

a finding with no rubric criterion is a missing element, and a missing
element is content — and prints the whole excluded set on every run rather
than dropping it.

G4 and G5 are EMPTY and stay empty. Both require a named human — brief §11
says so of G5 in as many words ('Not an agent'), and gate.mjs enforces `by`
and `date` on both. No agent may create them. Writing a plausible name into
either field would be the one edit that defeats the gate, so the foundations
round reports FAILED on exactly those two conditions and on nothing else.
That is the honest ceiling of an agent-run round, and it is where VD.2 stops.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash

findings.location: hero, between the H1 hash line and the trace card
findings.finding: The hero carries only the truncated hash, a 'Succeeded' pill and the full hash string. Age is absent from the page entirely, the finality badge appears only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid rather than in the hero, and the full hash at y approx 288 has no copy affordance of any kind.

findings.location: Overview grid, rows BLOCK through COST · MANA
findings.finding: The grid has six rows: BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET, COST · MANA. Value, nonce and transaction type are absent as labelled rows, and COST · MANA is a resource limit/usage pair, not the required fee breakdown, so no fee figure appears anywhere on the page.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note box below the SELECTOR / RAW table
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path shows raw bytes plus the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' set as ordinary body prose. There is no 'supply an ABI' action - no button, no link, no distinguishing type treatment - so the required affordance is present only as a description of one.

findings.location: hero, H1 hash line and the full-hash line 30px below it
findings.finding: The H1 truncates the hash to 10+8 characters at ~32px, and the complete 66-character hash is then set immediately beneath it at ~14px. The visually dominant instance is the incomplete one and the truncation buys nothing. The breadcrumb above truncates the same hash again at 6+4, so one identifier appears at three different lengths inside 130 vertical pixels with no single truncation rule.

findings.location: hero, 'Succeeded' badge to the right of the H1
findings.finding: The status badge is the smallest type in the hero at roughly 11px, set beside a ~32px H1. Status is the second most important fact on a transaction page and on a product whose reason to exist is reverted transactions; at this weight the hierarchy says the hash matters and the outcome is an annotation.

findings.location: Overview grid, COST · MANA value cell
findings.finding: '42000 / 100000 mana(FeeJuice)' sets the two figures, the unit and the token name at one monospace size, weight and colour, so the unit reads as more identifier. The digits carry no thousands grouping, and there is no space before '(FeeJuice)'. The unit and token should drop to the secondary text level so the numbers are the scannable part.

findings.location: hero, full-hash line at y approx 288
findings.finding: The full hash is set at the same size, weight, colour and face as a value cell in the Overview grid and carries no label. Typographically it reads as an orphaned table value that lost its row rather than as the page's canonical identifier.

findings.location: H1 versus the six section headings (Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes, Raw (chain-native))
findings.finding: The H1 is monospace while every section heading is the proportional sans. The page's top heading level therefore does not sit on the same scale as its second level, and the six section headings are the only true heading rung the eye can navigate by.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, JSON block
findings.finding: The JSON is set at roughly 13px on a ~1.55 line-height, barely denser than the 14px body around it. This is the one product-register element on a web-register page and the density difference should look chosen; at present it reads as the same rhythm on a grey surface.

findings.location: 'Raw (chain-native)' section heading
findings.finding: The parenthetical qualifier is set at the same size and weight as the heading noun, so 'chain-native' competes with 'Raw' for the scanning eye. Every other section heading is a single word or short phrase, making this one visually the longest and heaviest.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector

findings.location: hero, y163-296 (breadcrumb to full hash line)
findings.finding: The hero shows status ('Succeeded' badge at x843-1015) and the full hash (y284, x505-904) but omits three required items: the age, the finality badge, and any copy affordance beside the full hash. Finality is present only as a 'Pending' row inside the Overview grid at y874-915, which is not the hero.

findings.location: Overview grid (y791-1039), Decoded input note (y1325-1402), Raw block (y2351-2522)
findings.finding: Required data is absent. The Overview grid has only six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana) - no value, no nonce, no transaction type, no fee breakdown. Decoded input states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' as prose with no action control. The Raw block contains a single 5-line transaction object and no receipt payload, and the two payloads are not labelled or distinguished.

findings.location: all six section headings (Overview y742, Decoded input y1169, Events y1534, Internal calls y1790, State changes y2046, Raw y2301)
findings.finding: Every section heading is equidistant between the divider above it and the content below it: rule-to-heading is 28-30px and heading-to-content is 25-30px at all six sections (e.g. rule y712 -> 'Overview' y742 = 29px; heading bottom y760 -> table top y791 = 30px). No heading is bound by proximity to the block it labels, so across eight sections in one scroll the page reads as an evenly spaced strip of rules and items rather than six titled sections.

findings.location: right edge of the content column, whole page
findings.finding: Two container widths alternate down the right edge. Section rules, the Overview table, the Decoded-input table and the Raw block all end at x=1415 (911px wide); the trace card and all four notice boxes end at x=1203 (699px wide). The step repeats five times, and inside a single section - Decoded input - the table ending at 1415 sits 23px above a note ending at 1203, a 212px jog within one section.

findings.location: section aprons, y1503-2171 (Events, Internal calls, State changes)
findings.finding: The spacing apron is identical regardless of what the section holds: 100-101px above each rule, ~29px rule-to-heading, ~28px heading-to-content, for a 249px Overview table and for a 76-77px one-sentence notice alike. Events, Internal calls and State changes therefore consume 668px of vertical scroll to deliver three single sentences. The amount of space is not readable as a decision.

findings.location: trace card, hairline divider at y544
findings.finding: The divider inside the trace card runs x529-1138 while the card's content box runs x529-1178 (border 504-1203, padding 25px, confirmed by the Generate trace button's left edge at x529). It is inset 25px on the left and 65px on the right, so the only rule inside the page's most prominent card is visibly asymmetric.

findings.location: Overview table (x504-1415) and Decoded-input table (x504-1415)
findings.finding: Both tables are stretched to the column rather than sized to their data. The Overview table's longest value ends at x=1042, leaving a 373px dead column to the right of every row; the Decoded-input table's longest value ends at x=772, leaving 643px. At 1920 this is the wide viewport being consumed rather than used.

findings.location: boundary between the trace card (bottom border y620) and the first section rule (y712)
findings.finding: That gap is 92px, where every other section boundary measures 100-101px (y1039->1139, y1402->1503, y1658->1759, y1915->2016, y2171->2272). The one boundary that separates the hero from the body is the tightest on the page, by 9px.

findings.location: Overview grid, value column, rows Canonical (y832-874) and Finality (y874-915)
findings.finding: The two status badges have their box left edge at x=680 while every text value in the same column begins at x=689/690. The badge label is optically aligned but the badge box overhangs, so the value column's visible left edge ripples by 9px twice down six rows.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
raw section: the receipt payload, and labelling distinguishing transaction from receipt
decoded input: the 'supply an ABI' action (prose only, no control)

findings.location: hero, the H1 hash and the full hash line beneath it (y≈240–290)
findings.finding: No age and no finality badge appear in the hero — finality is only present as a 'Pending' row in the Overview grid — and neither the truncated H1 nor the full hash carries any copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost · Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent entirely.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains only a five-line transaction-shaped object (aztec.kind, aztec.contract). The receipt payload is absent and the two payloads are neither labelled nor distinguishable, so 'transaction and receipt JSON verbatim' is not satisfied.

findings.location: Decoded input section, note panel below the selector/raw rows
findings.finding: The unknown-selector path renders the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' but no 'supply an ABI' control — the specified action exists only as prose.

findings.location: trace card (hero, y≈340–615) vs Overview table vs Raw block
findings.finding: Three unrelated containment idioms on one page: the trace card has no border and is bounded only by a diffuse shadow; the Overview table and the Events/Internal-calls/State-changes panels use a ~#A2A2A2 1px hairline; the Raw block is a bare #ECECEB fill. There is no surface/elevation ladder, and the card carrying the primary action is the least-defined surface on the page.

findings.location: 'Succeeded' badge (hero) and 'Canonical: Yes' badge (Overview row 2) vs 'On demand' badge (trace card)
findings.finding: The page's single green role (#DCFCE7 / #166534) carries two different meanings — execution status and a boolean registry fact — while the trace-availability badge, the state the whole page turns on, is the only badge with no hue at all: a neutral dark dot on white with a hairline. Colour weight is allocated inversely to consequence.

findings.location: breadcrumb, 'TRANSACTION' eyebrow, Overview label column, the three explanation panels, footer
findings.finding: The text-emphasis ladder is compressed to #101010 / #242424 / #484848 / #565656. #484848 alone carries breadcrumb, eyebrow, grid labels, all explanatory prose and the footer, and #565656 is only 1.24:1 from it, so the last two levels are indistinguishable and colour does almost no hierarchy work.

findings.location: section rules between Overview / Decoded input / Events / Internal calls / State changes / Raw, and the header separator
findings.finding: Structural rules are #C8C8C8 on white — 1.86:1, below the 3:1 non-text floor — and the panel hairlines are ~2.6:1, so the page's containment is carried entirely by boundaries that are near-invisible on a bright display.

findings.location: whole page palette
findings.finding: The palette is stock framework values — pure neutral greys plus indigo-600 (#4F46E5) and green-100/800 — and the accent appears only twice (Generate trace fill, link colour). The theme reads as defaults not yet replaced rather than a designed light palette with an identity.

missing: hero: copy affordance on the full hash
hero: finality badge (Finality appears only as a grid row, not in the hero)
overview grid: fee breakdown (only a cost/limit usage row is shown)
decoded input: 'supply an ABI' action for the unknown selector
raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON

findings.location: hero (y≈240–290), overview grid (six rows, y≈795–1037), decoded-input section, raw section
findings.finding: Required facts are absent: the hero shows the full hash with no copy affordance and carries no age and no finality badge; the overview grid has only BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, FEE PAYER, TARGET and COST·MANA — no value, nonce, transaction type or fee breakdown; the decoded-input section states 'Supplying an ABI decodes them' in prose but offers no 'supply an ABI' control; the raw section shows one four-key transaction object and no receipt payload.

findings.location: whole page — content column spans x≈500–1415 of a 1920 px viewport
findings.finding: The wide viewport buys the page nothing. A single ~915 px column is used at every viewport, so roughly 1000 px of horizontal space is unused while the page runs to 2785 px vertically for about fifteen facts. The overview grid's value column is ~730 px wide to hold a 42-character address and a three-character 'Yes' badge; the decoded-input grid's value column holds '0x1a2b3c4d' and '0x' in the same 730 px. A two-column overview grid, or sections paired side by side, would put the whole factual payload in one screen.

findings.location: section separators between Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes and Raw (rules at y≈707, 1135, 1504, 1752, 2010, 2256)
findings.finding: Section spacing is uniform regardless of section weight: each section ends ~100 px above its following rule and rules sit ~180–430 px apart whether the section holds a six-row table or a single sentence. Events, Internal calls and State changes are three near-identical one-sentence notices, each in a 700×~75 px card, spread across ~750 px of scroll — three facts for two-thirds of a screen. The gaps do not encode grouping, so the page reads as long rather than as structured.

findings.location: trace card (y≈348–608) and the Events / Internal calls / State changes notice cards versus the overview grid, decoded-input grid and raw block
findings.finding: Two content widths coexist in one scroll: the notice and trace cards end at x≈1195 while the grids, the raw block and the section rules run to x≈1405–1415. The 210 px difference leaves a ragged right edge on five of the eight sections and gives the eye no single right margin to scan against.

findings.location: decoded-input grid, RAW row (y≈1265)
findings.finding: The RAW row's value is the two characters '0x' — an empty calldata payload rendered as a full-height grid row. At realistic volume this section will hold a long hex string in the same cell, so this capture does not exercise the section's density case at all; a reviewer cannot judge the wrapping strategy from it.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Overview grid: fee breakdown (fee amount, not only mana cost/limit)

findings.location: hero, beside the truncated hash and the full hash line below it
findings.finding: The hero carries only a 'Succeeded' chip. Age is absent from the hero and from the entire page, the finality badge appears only as a row inside the Overview grid, and the full hash on the second line has no copy affordance.

findings.location: Overview grid
findings.finding: The grid has six rows (Block, Canonical, Finality, Fee payer, Target, Cost·Mana). Value, nonce and transaction type are absent, and there is no fee amount — only a mana cost/limit pair, which is the resource-usage requirement, not the fee breakdown.

findings.location: Decoded input section, notice panel below the Selector/Raw rows
findings.finding: For an unknown selector the spec requires raw bytes AND a 'supply an ABI' action. Only the sentence 'Supplying an ABI decodes them.' is present; there is no control to supply one, so the page describes an affordance it does not offer.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section
findings.finding: The block contains one four-line transaction object under an 'aztec' key. The receipt payload is absent and neither payload is labelled, so the section cannot be read as 'transaction and receipt, verbatim'.

findings.location: trace card (hero) versus the notice panels in Events, Internal calls and State changes
findings.finding: The page's primary action sits inside a bordered rounded panel that is the same shared primitive as the three 'nothing here yet' notices below it. The container that carries the product's most important control is visually indistinguishable from the container that carries its absences.

findings.location: trace card line 'Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.' versus the Internal calls and State changes panels
findings.finding: One fact, two vocabularies: the trace card says data 'comes from' the execution trace while both section panels say it is 'read from' it. The specified sentence is a shared primitive and its two paraphrases below make the page read as written by two hands.

findings.location: Events notice panel, and the trace card body copy
findings.finding: Internal architecture leaks into visitor-facing copy: 'once this chain's receipts are published to the data plane this page reads' (Events) and 'runs it again under the recorder' (trace card). Both name implementation surfaces a visitor has no model for, in a register that is otherwise plain-spoken.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) section, the grey preformatted block
findings.finding: The one product-register element on the page is rendered as plain near-black monospace on a flat grey fill with no CodeTracer editor tokens, no panel header and no copy control. The product's single sanctioned register crossing is not made here, so the page's only code reads as an inert slab rather than as CodeTracer.

findings.location: trace card, primary button label 'Generate trace'
findings.finding: The primary action is labelled with a different verb from the product's signature 'Debug' used everywhere a transaction appears. The on-demand state justifies a distinct label, but nothing on the page ties 'Generate trace' back to debugging, so the page's strongest control does not read as the product's one promise.

findings.location: trace card body copy, clause 'it takes a moment, it needs an account'
findings.finding: Three unlike facts — a duration, an account requirement and a privacy claim — are strung into one sentence at equal weight, so the only one with a consequence for the visitor is the least prominent. 'A moment' is also the page's one unquantified quantity.

findings.location: footer, second line
findings.finding: 'Rendered from demo data (blocktracer-demo-gen)' sets the right honest tone but exposes an internal package name in monospace on a public surface; the human-readable half of the sentence already carries the meaning.

missing: Hero: copy affordance on the full hash
Hero: finality badge (rendered in the Overview grid instead)
Raw section: the chain-native receipt JSON (only a single unlabelled transaction object is shown)

findings.location: Overview section, the six-row fact grid below the trace card (y approx 790-1030)
findings.finding: The Overview grid carries six rows where Page-Descriptions 7.2 names eight facts: value, fee breakdown, nonce and transaction type are all absent, and their place is taken by CANONICAL and FINALITY badge rows (FINALITY being a hero requirement demoted into the grid). The omission is not a data limit - the raw block further down the page exposes "kind": "public-avm-call", so the transaction type is available and simply was never given a labelled row. The narrow 130px label column against an ~800px value column leaves every row two-thirds empty, confirming visually that the grid was populated from whatever the adapter exposed rather than from the specified fact set.

missing: A timeline or scrubber expressing position within the trace

findings.location: identity bar, between the fourth stepping-button pair (x≈655) and the phase rail (x≈780)
findings.finding: There is no timeline or scrubber. Position in the trace is expressed only by the numeric fraction '128 / 1315'; there is no track, no tick run and no playhead in the bar, and no time surface in any pane. The Code pane's 'Iteration 3 of 8' strip is a scrubber over one loop, not over the trace. The expectation block lists the position readout and the timeline as separate required items, so the fraction does not satisfy this one. Note that the bar has ~285px of unused space between the rail and the 'NOIR' tag, so the removal is not forced by width at this viewport.

findings.location: provenance banner, the four prose lines under the 'Synthetic demo data' badge
findings.finding: The banner's prose is the largest and most loosely set type on the page — roughly 15px at ~1.6 line-height over four lines — which makes it typographically senior to every pane title, to the '128 / 1315' position readout and to all session content. In the tool register the boilerplate now outranks the session. One step down the scale and one step tighter on leading would restore the ranking without dropping a word.

findings.location: Code pane, source listing, lines 26–46
findings.finding: Line pitch is ~24px on ~13px monospace (≈1.85), which is web-body leading in a code listing: twenty lines fill 488px where the desktop app's density would show roughly half again as many. This is the rare density finding whose fix shows MORE information, not less.

findings.location: identity bar hash vs. Transaction pane hero/FEE PAYER/TARGET vs. Call Trace frame column
findings.finding: Three truncation strategies for one data type on one screen. The identity bar middle-truncates ('0xb63616…6359'); the Transaction pane hard-wraps the same 66-character hash over three lines and wraps FEE PAYER and TARGET to three lines each with two-character orphans ('32', '4c') on the last; the Call Trace truncates from the right, so 'zk_shields · src/shi…' discards the filename, which is the only part that distinguishes one frame's file from another's. Right-truncating a path removes exactly the informative tail.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge (x≈680): lines 26, 40, 41
findings.finding: Source lines are cut at the pane border with no ellipsis and no visible horizontal-scroll affordance — line 40 stops at 'remaining_shiel', line 41 at 'after each', line 26 at 'initial_shield, re'. The explanatory note above them runs into the same border ('…the lines above it are not in' / 'this window.'). Invisible truncation makes a partial line read as a complete one, which in a code listing is a correctness problem, not a cosmetic one.

findings.location: Code pane, loop strip at y≈293
findings.finding: Four typographic treatments in one 20px row: 'LOOP' in tracked grey caps, 'iterate_asteroids' in mono, 'line 4' as an underlined link, and 'Iteration 3 of 8' in a large dark UI weight that is the boldest, largest text in the pane — heavier than the pane's own 'CODE' title. The strip's most prominent phrase is its least specific one, and the row reads as four unrelated objects rather than one caption.

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail 'FETCHING / OPENING / POSITIONING' (x≈780–1030)
findings.finding: The three chips are identical in size, weight and tracking, so which phase is in progress is carried by fill alone and the rail is not readable without reading it. A weight or case step on the active chip would let the rail be scanned at a glance, which is the whole purpose of a rail over a sentence.

findings.location: Values pane, 'masses' row (y≈752–770)
findings.finding: The array literal wraps, but the continuation ('14]') is not aligned to the value column's left edge and the type cell '[Field; 8]' stays on the first line, so a single row reads as two ragged half-rows and the value/type columns lose their shared baseline for that entry alone.

findings.location: identity bar, 'NOIR' tag at x≈1330
findings.finding: The language tag is set in small grey caps that match no other level in the bar and carries no adjacent label, so beside the two icon buttons it reads as a stray token rather than as the session's source language. It is correct that it is here; it is not typographically placed.

missing: A timeline or scrubber expressing position within the trace

findings.location: identity bar, between the fourth stepping-button pair (x≈655) and the phase rail (x≈780)
findings.finding: No timeline or scrubber is laid out anywhere on the page. The bar runs straight from the last button pair to the '128 / 1315' readout to the phase rail, and no pane carries a time surface. The Code pane's 'Iteration 3 of 8' tick strip spans one loop, not the trace. The bar is a single row at this viewport with roughly 285px of empty space between the rail and the 'NOIR' tag — more than a 160px track would need — so the element is absent by layout decision rather than by shortfall.

findings.location: Call Trace tabbed region, below the 'By call order. / Self cost' footer (y≈505) down to the region border (y≈620)
findings.finding: The measurement the change has not made: the region runs y≈246–620 (374px) and its content — seven frames ending at y≈480 plus the footer at y≈493 — stops at y≈505, leaving about 115px, roughly 31% of the region, permanently empty. Directly below it the Values pane (y≈630–900) is clipping its ninth row at the viewport edge. The height belongs to the Values pane, not the tabbed region; the split should be driven by content or the region should shrink to fit.

findings.location: provenance banner, y≈30–185
findings.finding: The banner occupies about 185px — 21% of a 900px viewport — for a four-line paragraph whose measure is roughly 600px, so about 840px of the band is empty to the right of the text and 185 rows come out of the pane column that is simultaneously cutting rows off at the bottom. The band is sanctioned; its vertical cost at this viewport is not paid for. Setting the prose in two columns beside the badge, or reclaiming the leading, would return most of it.

findings.location: identity bar, between the phase rail (ends x≈1030) and the 'NOIR' tag (x≈1330)
findings.finding: A ~285px void splits the bar into two clusters — everything session-related packed into the left 1030px, two icon actions and a tag stranded at the right edge. Proximity therefore groups the actions with nothing, and the bar reads as a strip of unrelated objects at its right end while its left end is dense. Either the actions move in against the rail or the gap is filled by the element that used to occupy it.

findings.location: bottom of the pane column: Values pane 'regeneration' row and Transaction pane 'RAW' row at y≈890
findings.finding: The pane column does not resolve at the viewport edge. The Values pane's last row and the Transaction pane's 'RAW' row are sliced horizontally by y=900 with no pane bottom border and no visible scroll affordance in either, while the Code pane closes with a border just above. Three panes in one row ending at three different vertical positions, one of them mid-row, reads as clipping rather than as scrolling.

findings.location: Code pane, right border (x≈680), lines 26, 40, 41 and the '+3' chip at y≈423
findings.finding: Content meets the pane border with no right gutter: lines 40 and 41 are cut flush against the border, and line 26's inline value chip '+3' is pushed off its own line onto a half-row at y≈423 between rows 26 and 27, breaking the listing's line grid. The overflow is unindicated — no ellipsis, no fade, no horizontal scrollbar — so the pane's right edge is doing the truncation silently.

findings.location: top-left of the page: pane column border (x≈8), banner badge and prose (x≈10–12), identity bar back-link (x≈20)

findings.location: column widths: Code ≈674px, nav column ≈456px, Transaction pane ≈278px

The Transaction pane is the narrowest column and holds the longest values, so every 66-character identifier wraps to three lines with a two-character last line, while the Code pane — the widest — still clips its own source at its border, meaning the extra width it holds does not buy it a complete line anyway. At this viewport the Code pane is the pane that should lose width first, and it is the one that loses it last.

findings.location: Values pane, 'masses' row (y≈745–780)

missing: A timeline or scrubber expressing position within the trace

findings.location: identity bar, between the fourth stepping-button pair (x≈655) and the phase rail (x≈780)
findings.finding: No timeline or scrubber is present: there is no track, no elapsed run and no playhead in the bar, and no pane carries a time surface. findings.location: amber: 'Partial' badge (identity bar x≈205 and Transaction pane hero y≈289) vs. changed values in the Values pane ('9000' y≈702, '2000' y≈869, their left row-markers) and the 'damage: 0→2000' chip in the Code pane (y≈559)
findings.finding: One hue, two roles. Amber marks the transaction's outcome ('Partial') and simultaneously marks 'this value changed at this step'. A reader who has learned amber = changed in the Values pane meets the same amber as a status badge in the bar and in the metadata pane. The changed role is the one that must stay unambiguous because it is read at every step; the outcome badge should move to the status family it belongs to.

findings.location: blue: 'line 4' (Code pane y≈293), 'Self cost' (Call Trace footer y≈493), '101:0' (Transaction pane y≈409), the 'FETCHING' phase chip (identity bar x≈782), and the 'Synthetic demo data' badge (banner y≈52)
findings.finding: The blue family carries three meanings at once: the hyperlink role, the engine's active-phase chip, and a provenance badge that is neither a link nor a status. The badge is the worst of the three — outlined and tinted in the same blue family as every hyperlink on the page, positioned first in the reading order, and not interactive. Provenance is a content classification and needs a hue that is not spoken for by navigation or by engine state.

findings.location: Code pane loop strip, tick '3' (x≈463, y≈293), against the current source line (y≈562) and the current Call Trace frame (y≈443)

The current loop iteration is marked instead by a thin dark underline on a neutral grey fill — the same neutral as the two already-elapsed ticks — so the one remaining time-like surface on the page uses neither the position colour nor a distinct elapsed colour. Ticks 1–2 (elapsed) and tick 3 (current) differ only by an underline.

findings.location: muted grey text: Code pane note 'Showing from line 26 — …' (y≈357), Transaction pane note 'aztec private function executed client-side; …' (y≈742), Call Trace footer 'By call order.' (y≈493), the 'ACIR opcodes' column header (y≈291)
findings.finding: One muted grey serves both decorative labels and load-bearing sentences. The two notes are the only place the page explains why the listing starts at line 26 and why the private half has no call structure, yet they are tinted identically to a column header and a sort caption, at the page's smallest size. Nothing in the emphasis scale separates text a reader must read from text they can skip, so the two sentences that carry unique information sit at the bottom of the hierarchy.

findings.location: surface levels: provenance banner (y≈30–185), identity bar (y≈190–240), pane interiors
findings.finding: The banner, the identity bar and the pane bodies are all the same white; only hairlines distinguish three functionally different zones, and the only tonal step in the theme is the faint fill on the pane header strips. The light theme is therefore carried almost entirely by borders, which is the signature of a dark theme lightened rather than a light theme designed — the dark build has surface-raised/sunken levels doing this work, and here they have collapsed to one level.

findings.location: identity bar, the four stepping-button pairs (x≈370–660)
findings.finding: The four pairs do not read as one state. The first pair's glyphs are visibly darker than the three pairs to their right, so with the engine still in 'FETCHING' the group looks partly live and partly not. If all four are disabled until the engine is up they should share one disabled tint; if only some are, the difference needs to be legible as a decision rather than as a rendering variance.

findings.location: identity bar, 'NOIR' tag at x≈1330
findings.finding: The language tag is the lowest-contrast text in the bar, tinted at roughly the same level as the dimmed stepping glyphs beside it, so a permanent property of the session is rendered at the emphasis level the page uses for unavailable controls. It is correct that it is present on this view; it is coloured as though it were inert.

missing: A timeline or scrubber expressing position within the trace.

findings.location: identity bar, between the last stepping group (x≈600-655) and the `128 / 1315` readout (x≈672-757)
findings.finding: No timeline and no scrubber is rendered at 1440. The only expression of position in the trace is the numeric fraction `128 / 1315`, and a fraction is a readout, not a timeline: nothing on the page draws WHERE step 128 falls in 1,315, so proportional position — the one fact a stepping surface exists to keep in view — cannot be read at a glance. It is present at the wide viewport, which makes this a viewport-conditional drop rather than a design that never had one, and it is the wrong thing to have dropped: the bar retains a 3-chip phase rail (x≈785-1030), a language tag and two action marks, all of which are stated or reachable elsewhere, while the element that expresses the session's own coordinate is the one removed. Either restore a capped-width position graphic at this width or amend the expectation; as captured the view does not show a required element.

findings.location: navigation column: Call Trace region (y 245-630) versus Values pane (y 637-900)
findings.finding: The call-trace region is 385px tall. Seven frames end at y≈480, the `By call order. / Self cost` footer sits at y≈493, and everything from y≈505 to y≈628 — 123px, 32% of the region — is blank. The Values pane immediately below gets 263px, shows nine rows, and is cut mid-row at the viewport bottom (`regeneration 1000` sliced) with further values unreachable. That is the answer to the open measurement: the Values pane should have the height. Seven frames fill barely half the region they are given, while the value list already overflows and a real Noir frame has dozens of locals. Let the tabbed region size toward its content with a floor and give the remainder to Values.

findings.location: provenance banner, y 0-178
findings.finding: The banner takes 178px — 20% of a 900px viewport, about seven code rows or seven call-trace frames — before the identity bar starts. The cost is not the content, which is required, but the layout: four lines of prose set at a ~580px measure inside a 1440px band, leaving roughly 850x130px of the band blank. The same sentences at a 1000-1100px measure are two lines; badge, slug and two lines lands near 110px and returns ~65px to a pane column that is currently clipping all three of its panes at the viewport bottom. This is the register's scarcest resource being spent on the widest whitespace on the page.

findings.location: Code pane header stack, y 245-390 (pane title, LOOP/iteration row, file-tab strip, two-line prose note)
findings.finding: Four stacked bands and ~145px — 22% of the pane's 655px, about six code lines — sit above the first code line, in a pane whose content is cut mid-glyph at line 46 by the viewport bottom. Twenty-one code lines are visible. The band carrying the least is the two-line sentence at y≈357-375, `Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.`, which restates what the line-number gutter already states and is the only one of the four with no navigation in it; the other three (iteration selector, file tabs, LOOP context) all earn their rows. Folding that sentence into the gutter or the pane title returns code lines at the viewport where they are scarcest.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge (x≈680) on lines 26, 40 and 41
findings.finding: Long lines are hard-cut at the pane border with no ellipsis, no fade and no visible overflow affordance: line 26 stops at `calculate_remaining_shield_pct(initial_shield, re`, line 40 at `fn calculate_shield_regeneration(initial_shield:Field, remaining_shiel`, line 41 mid-comment at `after each`. A reader cannot distinguish a truncated line from a complete one, which matters most on line 40 — a signature whose remaining parameters are simply not indicated. At 675px the Code pane is the first thing this viewport starves, so the truncation is expected; the absence of any mark for it is not.

findings.location: Transaction pane, hash header (y≈289) and the FEE PAYER (y≈503-545) and TARGET (y≈572-618) rows
findings.finding: The metadata column is ~280px and spends nine rows on values it states twice or breaks badly. The transaction hash appears truncated as `0xb636167a…66d46359` in the pane header and then again in full on the two rows immediately below it. FEE PAYER and TARGET each wrap a 20-byte value across three lines whose last line carries two characters (`32`, `4c`), so each costs three rows and neither can be compared against another address at a glance. One data type is given three different treatments on one screen — middle ellipsis in the identity bar, middle ellipsis in this pane's header, and a ragged three-line wrap two rows later — and the most expensive treatment is the least legible, in the pane whose bottom row is already clipped.

findings.location: Values pane, `masses` row (y≈745-785)
findings.finding: One row is three lines tall because its array literal `[100, 2000, 200, 100, 100, 50, 50, 14]` wraps, setting a row height triple its neighbours' ~25px in a pane that is already cut off at the viewport bottom. The row's own right-hand cell already carries `[Field; 8]`, so the length is stated independently of the literal; eliding to one line with the full value on demand costs the reader nothing and returns two value rows.

findings.location: bottom edge of all three columns at y=900 (Code line 46, Values `regeneration`, Transaction `RAW`)
findings.finding: No column draws a bottom border or any scroll affordance; all three simply stop at the viewport edge with a half-height row sliced mid-glyph. The shell no longer overhangs, which is the fix that mattered, but the result still gives a reader no way to tell 'there is more, scroll' from 'this was clipped'. A bottom rule on the pane column, or a half-row fade, would make the truncation a statement rather than an artefact.

missing: A timeline or scrubber expressing position within the trace.

findings.location: identity bar, between the stepping groups (ending x≈655) and the `128 / 1315` readout (x≈672)
findings.finding: There is no timeline and no scrubber on this surface. Position in the trace is stated only as a fraction. Beyond the presence rule, this is the sharpest continuity break with the CodeTracer desktop application on the page: the timeline is one of the tool's signature primitives, it is what a returning desktop user looks for first to orient inside a 1,315-step recording, and a web session that prints a fraction instead is a reinterpretation that has to be relearned. It is also inconsistent within this product — the same view renders one at the wide viewport — so the primitive exists and is being withheld at the width most laptops will open the product at.

findings.location: provenance banner, y 0-178, above the identity bar
findings.finding: The banner belongs here and its content is right, but it is drawn in the explorer register: a rounded pill badge, four lines of body-face prose set at a ~580px measure with marketing leading, and 178px of band — 20% of the viewport — before any tool chrome appears. Nothing else on the page is set that way; the panes below it are dense, small-type and hairline-bounded. The first screenful therefore opens as a web page and becomes a debugger only at y=186, which inverts the deliberate, visible transition §3 asks for at this boundary. Set the sentences at the band's own width, in the pane type scale, with the badge and slug on the same line, and the banner reads as the tool's own statement rather than as a section pasted in from the marketing surface.

findings.location: Transaction pane, `Status reason` row, y≈352-393
findings.finding: The row reads `Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded` — a raw wire enum, in kebab case, wrapped over two lines, presented as user-facing copy. Every other sentence on this page is written in product English, including the paragraph six rows below it (`aztec private function executed client-side; only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are published — no call structure to trace`), which is exactly the tone this product's copy is meant to have. One row leaks the serialisation vocabulary into the surface, and it is the row explaining a `Partial` outcome, so it is the row a confused reader goes to. Say it in words: the private part succeeded and the public part succeeded.

findings.location: identity bar, far right: the two action marks at x≈1360-1415 versus the eight stepping buttons at x≈370-655
findings.finding: One class of affordance is drawn in two shapes on one strip. The eight stepping controls are square-cornered glyph buttons; the share and download actions immediately to their right are circles, and they are the only circular elements anywhere on the page. Whatever the rank difference between stepping and exporting, it should not be carried by a shape the rest of the product does not use — the circles read as borrowed chrome sitting at the end of the tool's own control strip.

findings.location: `Partial` badge, identity bar x≈205 and Transaction pane header x≈1188
findings.finding: The same outcome badge appears twice on one screen at two sizes and two weights, 1,180px apart. The duplication itself is defensible — the bar states identity, the pane states metadata — but the two instances should be one primitive at one size, and here the pane's copy is visibly the larger and heavier of the two, which ranks the metadata restatement above the identity bar's.

findings.location: phase rail, identity bar x≈785-1030 (`FETCHING` chip active)
findings.finding: The rail marks FETCHING as the phase in progress while every pane around it is fully populated — code at the pinned line, seven frames, eleven values. That is truthful for a still frame whose engine has not loaded, and the rail is the right vocabulary for saying it, but nothing else on the surface carries the same message: the eight stepping buttons beside it do not read as inert at a glance, so the honest fact has to be inferred from a three-word chip. The rail's claim and the controls' state should read as one statement, not two.

findings.location: Code pane, line 41 comment in `src/shield.nr`
findings.finding: The fixture's own source comment reads `// shields regain a percentage of the maxium capacity after each …` — `maxium` for `maximum`. The demo tree is authored content and this listing is the flagship surface's centrepiece, so the typo is the product's copy, not a user's. It is one character in a fixture and costs nothing to fix.

findings.location: provenance banner, the full-width band above the identity bar — roughly the top 160 px of the 1080 px viewport, prose column ending near x=600
findings.finding: The banner is correct as content and wrong as layout. It occupies about 160 px of 1080 — roughly 15% of the viewport, and about 30% of everything above the panes — while using only the leftmost ~600 px of a 1920 px band. Around two thirds of the band it claims is empty. The prose is set at explorer-register scale: four lines at ~22 px leading, against ~12 px identity-bar text and ~13 px pane rows a few pixels below it. That is marketing-grade padding sitting directly on top of a tool surface, which is the B1 failure verbatim — space spent where it buys nothing while the content it displaces is scrolled. The displacement is visible in the same frame: the Code pane clips line 54 at the viewport edge, the Transaction pane's RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) JSON is cut mid-object at `"transfer"`, and the Values pane ends flush against the bottom with `i` as its last visible row. The banner's own expectation block anticipates this — it is full-width by design and the rows come out of the panes — so the question it poses is whether the rows are earned, and at this measurement they are not. Nothing about the banner's honesty function requires four stacked lines in a 600 px measure; the same badge, slug and sentences flowed across the full band at pane-body scale would cost roughly 80 px instead of 160 and return that height to the region that is currently truncating a JSON object. It is not P1: the banner is present, legible, correctly toned and correctly placed first in the shell. It is P2 because the register's own rubric names this exact trade, and on this page the trade is currently being lost.

findings.location: numeric columns across all four panes: call trace opcode column vs. identity bar readout, Transaction pane COST · MANA row, Values pane value column
findings.finding: Thousands separators are applied in exactly one place. The call trace right column reads 1,315 and 1,208; the identity bar readout beside it prints the same magnitude as 128 / 1315; the Transaction pane's COST · MANA row reads 88000 / 200000; and every four-digit figure in Values (10000, 9000, 2000, 1000) is unseparated. The call trace's 1,315 and the identity bar's 1315 are the SAME number rendered two ways about 400 px apart, which is the pair a reader is most likely to compare. Pick one rule and apply it to every integer on the surface; if the intent was 'separators only above 9,999' then 1,315 is the outlier and should lose them.

findings.location: Transaction pane (right rail): FEE PAYER and TARGET value cells, vs. the pane's own badge row and the identity bar
findings.finding: Four truncation strategies for one data type. The identity bar elides 6+4 (0xb63616…6359); the Transaction pane badge row elides 8+8 (0xb636167a…66d46359); the line immediately beneath that badge prints the full 40-character value, so the 8+8 elision buys nothing and the same hash appears twice on consecutive lines at two sizes; and FEE PAYER and TARGET do not elide at all — they hard-wrap onto a second right-aligned line (…0184953e2a272b5 / e430d5d932 and …936f12e6fe8f17 / a59161624c), splitting mid-byte, so a reader cannot tell whether the second line is a continuation or a second field. In a product whose texture is hashes this is the single most visible typographic inconsistency on the page.

findings.location: provenance banner, full-width band above the identity bar
findings.finding: The disclaimer is set at the largest body size on the page with the loosest line-height, while the panes it sits above run at roughly 11–12 px. On a tool surface the type scale therefore peaks on the sentence a returning visitor reads once. Compounding it, the measure is held to about 600 px of a 1920 px viewport — roughly 65 characters — so four lines are used where two would fit comfortably at a 90–100 character measure, and those two extra rows plus the leading come out of the pane column (the band occupies ~180 px of 1080). Dropping the banner one step on the scale and widening the measure would keep every word and return height to Code and Values.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge at lines 40 and 53
findings.finding: Long source lines are hard-clipped mid-identifier at the pane boundary with no ellipsis, no fade and no visible horizontal scroll affordance: line 40 stops at `shield_regen_perce` and line 53 at `damage: Field, r`. Every other truncation on the page announces itself (the ellipsis in the hashes, the `+3` / `+2` overflow chips in this very pane's value gutter), so this one reads as a render fault rather than a deliberate cut. A gradient mask or a persistent thin scrollbar would make the cut legible as a cut.

findings.location: Transaction pane, the three-line paragraph under EXECUTIONS — 'aztec private function executed client-side; only proofs, nullifiers and commitments are published — no call structure to trace'
findings.finding: The most information-dense sentence in the pane is set at the smallest size on the page and at a dim emphasis level, over a measure of roughly 45 characters, so it breaks into three lines with tight leading. It explains why the private execution has no trace — the pane's least obvious fact — and it is typographically the pane's least prominent element, ranking below the CANONICAL / FINALITY badges that carry one word each. One step up in size and one step up in emphasis would cost no rows.

findings.location: Code pane, loop-context strip: 'LOOP iterate_asteroids  line 4  Iteration 3 of 8'
findings.finding: Three type treatments share one 20 px line with no clear primary: `LOOP` as a tracked uppercase label, `iterate_asteroids` as bold mono, `line 4` as an underlined sans link, and `Iteration 3 of 8` at a visibly larger size than any of them. The largest text in the strip is the least specific fact in it — the iteration count is already spelled out by the highlighted chip 3 in the 1–8 rail immediately to its right. Demote 'Iteration 3 of 8' to the label size and let the function name lead.

findings.location: Code pane, inline value chips on lines 27, 28, 32, 49 and 50
findings.finding: The chip notation mixes three forms within nine visible lines: `damage=0`, `shield_pct=90` and `mass=200` use `=`; line 32 uses a colon and an arrow, `damage: 0→2000`; line 50 pairs `result=90` with a bare `→90` chip carrying no name. If `=` means 'value here' and `→` means 'changed here', the colon in the changed form is the odd character out, and the unnamed `→90` chip on line 50 gives the reader no way to know which binding moved.

findings.location: call trace pane, column header row: 'FRAME' at left vs. 'ACIR opcodes' at right
findings.finding: The two headers of one table are cased differently. `FRAME` is tracked uppercase; opposite it `ACIR` is uppercase (correctly, as an acronym) but `opcodes` is lowercase, so the right header reads as an acronym followed by a stray word rather than as a peer column label. `ACIR OPCODES` in the same tracked uppercase, or 'Frame' / 'ACIR opcodes' in sentence case, would make it one header row.

findings.location: Transaction pane, 'Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded'
findings.finding: The slug wraps on one of its own internal hyphens, breaking after 'public-part-' so the second line opens with 'succeeded'. The line break is typographically indistinguishable from the hyphens that are part of the identifier, so a reader cannot recover the exact token. A slug is a single unit: set it in the mono face used for other machine values and break it with an explicit wrap marker, or let it overflow-wrap without landing on a hyphen.

findings.location: whole shell — `Partial` pills (identity bar and Transaction pane), Values rows `remaining_shield` 9000 / `damage` 2000, Code pane inline chips `damage: 0->2000` and `result=90 ->90`, numeric literals on lines 32 and 42
findings.finding: One amber carries three unrelated meanings: degraded trace status, changed-value diff, and editor numeric literal. Line 32 shows all three within a single row — the literal `100` in `mass * (100 - shield_pct)` and the chip `damage: 0->2000` are the same hue two centimetres apart, so the reader cannot tell an authored constant from a value that just changed. Give the diff role its own hue (or reserve amber for diff alone and move `Partial` to a distinct warning tone).

findings.location: identity bar, scrubber track (approx. x=700-935)
findings.finding: The unfilled portion of the scrubber track is a light mid-grey and is the brightest large object in the bar — brighter than the `Partial` badge and reading at roughly the weight of active text. An empty track carries no information yet draws the eye before the position readout `128 / 1315` immediately to its right. Drop the track to the bar's border value and let the fill be the only lit element.

findings.location: identity bar (scrubber fill, phase rail `FETCHING`), Code pane header `line 4`, Call Trace footer `Self cost`, Transaction pane `101:0`, provenance banner `Synthetic demo data` badge
findings.finding: Four cool accents inside roughly forty degrees of hue, each meaning something different: green-teal for scrubber fill, cyan for the active phase, blue for links, and the same blue again for the provenance badge. They read as accidents of four separate components rather than one accent family. Two consequences: the green fill implies 'done/ok' for a bar that only expresses position, and the provenance badge — the one element on this register that must not read as chrome — is coloured exactly like a hyperlink.

findings.location: tab strip `EVENT LOG`; Transaction pane label column `BLOCK` through `RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)`; Call Trace header `ACIR opcodes`; identity bar `OPENING` / `POSITIONING` / `NOIR`
findings.finding: The dimmest text tier sits at roughly 3:1 on the pane surface at 10-11px. The inactive `EVENT LOG` tab is the worst placement of it: that label is the sole affordance revealing the event log exists, and it is currently the least legible text in its region. The Transaction pane's label column is the key half of every key/value pair and is dimmer than the prose paragraphs below it. Raise the low-emphasis tier to clear 4.5:1; density is not the thing being traded away here, only luminance.

findings.location: identity bar, the four stepping-control groups between the `Partial` badge and the scrubber
findings.finding: All four groups render at two barely-separated greys and none carries an accent. With the engine mid-load (`Engine loading — 18 MB`, phase rail on FETCHING) there is no colour signal separating a control that is live from one that is inert, so the disabled state that the shell relies on to carry loading is not readable as a state. Reverse stepping — the product's premise — is also the same grey as everything else; it has no colour claim on the bar it lives in.

findings.location: Code pane, line 41 comment `// shields regain a percentage of the maxium capacity after each hit`
findings.finding: The only red on the entire screen is the comment colour. In a dark tool register red is the failure hue, and here it is spent on the lowest-priority text in the densest pane — a salmon comment pulls harder than the current-position row six lines below it. It also leaves nothing unclaimed for a divergent or failed trace, which would have to borrow amber, and amber is already carrying three jobs (finding 1). Move comments to a desaturated grey-green and hold red.

findings.location: Transaction pane — `Yes` (CANONICAL), `Safe` (FINALITY), `Not observable` (private execution), `Trace ready` (public execution)
findings.finding: One neutral grey outlined pill means both affirmation (`Yes`, `Safe`) and unavailability (`Not observable`), while `Trace ready` alone gets green. Scanning the pane by colour, a positive fact and a limitation are indistinguishable, and the single green makes the greys read as 'not ready' by contrast. Either give all four a role tone or give none of them one.

findings.location: provenance banner / identity bar boundary, and the gutters between the Code, Call Trace and Transaction panes
findings.finding: Surface levels are compressed: the banner, the identity bar and the inter-pane gutters all sit at essentially the same near-black, with pane bodies only a few points lighter. The provenance banner — this register's only device for saying whose data this is — is separated from the identity bar by a hairline alone and inherits the same surface, so it reads as the top of the chrome rather than as content. One more step of separation on the banner (or on the pane bodies) would make the shell's three levels legible without spending a pixel of pane height.

findings.location: centre column — Call Trace region (y≈250–745) and Values pane (y≈748–1080)
findings.finding: The navigation region ends at the seventh frame (y≈478) and its footer row 'By call order. / Self cost' (y≈493), leaving roughly 250px — about half the region — empty; the Values pane below ends at its last row 'i / 2 / u32' (y≈1011) with a further ~60px empty. That is ~310px of unused height, ~29% of the viewport, sitting in the one column whose content is complete, while the Code pane is scrolled (showing lines 26–54 of a longer file) and the Transaction pane is clipped mid-JSON at the bottom edge. The 3/5–2/5 split should be content-driven, or the slack should be given to a neighbour that is actually truncated.

findings.location: provenance banner, y≈0–185
findings.finding: The banner spends 185px — 17% of the viewport, about seven code rows or seven call-trace frames — to set four sentences at a ~370px measure inside a 1920px full-width band whose remaining ~1,500px is empty. The content is required and correct; the cost is not. Setting the same prose to a ~900px measure makes it two lines and returns ~55–60px to the panes below at no loss of information.

findings.location: Code pane, right edge x≈912, lines 40 and 53
findings.finding: Long lines are clipped flush against the pane border with no ellipsis, fade or horizontal scroll affordance: line 40 ends '…shield_regen_perce' and line 53 ends '…damage: Field, r'. A reader cannot tell whether the signature continues or the fixture is truncated. The Code pane holds 47% of the width and still cannot fit a signature, which makes the ~310px of vertical air in the column beside it read as a misallocation rather than breathing room.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER (y≈478–503) and TARGET (y≈529–554) rows

findings.location: provenance banner, y=0-180, above the identity bar

findings.location: pane headers across the four panes — 'CODE', the 'CALL TRACE / EVENT LOG' tab strip, 'VALUES', 'TRANSACTION'
findings.finding: Three header treatments in one row of panes: a plain uppercase title bar (Code, Values, Transaction), a two-tab strip with an underlined active tab, and — inside Code only — two further header rows (the LOOP/iteration strip and the file-tab row) styled unlike any other pane's chrome. findings.location: badges across the screen — 'Synthetic demo data' (banner), 'Partial' (identity bar and Transaction pane), 'Not observable' and 'Trace ready' (Transaction pane), 'NOIR' (identity bar right)
findings.finding: Five badge treatments coexist: an outlined blue pill, an outlined orange chip, a grey filled chip, a green filled chip and a bare letter-spaced uppercase mark. findings.location: identity bar, left cluster: the back link and chain slug

findings.location: Provenance banner, the full-width band at the top of the shell above the identity bar (y ≈ 0–186)
findings.finding: The banner is typeset to the explorer register inside the debugger register, and it is the only element on the page that is. It is 1920 px wide and its prose is confined to a 590 px measure at the far left, so about 69% of the band it charges for is blank; the four sentences run at explorer body size with roughly 22 px leading and sit inside ~40 px of top and ~34 px of bottom padding, none of which is the padding any pane on this page uses. The result is 186 px — 17% of the viewport, 22% of everything below the identity bar — spent on four short lines that the band's own width could carry in two at pane leading, for a reclaimable ~90 px. The brief makes the banner's presence and its full width non-negotiable and its content is not the complaint: the badge, the `aztec` slug and the sentences are exactly right, and the distinction they draw (synthetic hash, real recorded Noir trace) is the one thing no other surface in this register can say. The complaint is that the register's scarcest resource is rows and this is the largest single discretionary spend of them on the page, paid by the two panes that visibly clip: the Code pane cuts line 54 through the middle of its glyphs at the viewport edge, and the Transaction pane's RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block runs off the bottom mid-token. Four more code lines and three more JSON rows are the exact size of the margin. Nothing here needs to show less information; it needs to be laid out like the tool it sits on top of.

findings.location: Transaction pane — header 'TRANSACTION' versus its field labels BLOCK / CANONICAL / FINALITY / FEE PAYER / TARGET / COST · MANA / EXECUTIONS
findings.finding: One 10px letterspaced-uppercase style carries six different roles on this screen: pane title (CODE, VALUES, TRANSACTION), tab label (CALL TRACE, EVENT LOG), column header (FRAME), field label (BLOCK…RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE)), phase-rail step (FETCHING/OPENING/POSITIONING) and the NOIR language tag. Same size, same weight, same tracking, same grey. The consequence is visible in the Transaction pane: its title does not outrank the labels of its own rows, and the pane reads as a list of eleven equal labels of which the first happens to be the pane's name. Only the header's background tint separates them, so the hierarchy is carried by fill rather than by type.

findings.location: provenance banner, top of shell, x≈12–605, y≈78–160
findings.finding: The banner's four sentences are set at explorer-register scale — roughly 15px sans on ~22px leading over a ~600px measure — inside a register whose labels are ~10px and whose code is ~13px mono. It is the largest, darkest, longest continuous run of type on the page, so the first thing the eye resolves on a positioned debugger session is boilerplate, ahead of the identity bar and every pane title. This is not an argument for cutting a word: set at the debugger's own scale and leading the same four sentences occupy roughly two rows instead of four, and the rows return to the panes.

findings.location: call trace opcode column vs identity bar position readout vs Values pane vs Transaction pane COST · MANA row
findings.finding: Numeric formatting is not comparable across magnitudes. The call trace prints 1,315 and 1,208 with thousands separators; the identity bar prints what is evidently the same total as 1315 in '128 / 1315'; the Values pane prints 10000, 9000, 2000, 1000 bare; COST · MANA prints '88000 / 200000'. Three conventions for the same magnitude class on one screen, and the two forms of 1315 sit 600px apart in the same horizontal band.

findings.location: Code pane, notice row above line 26

It is also an ~85-character monospace measure, which is long for a mono line. Only the grey band separates it from the code.

findings.location: Code pane header strip, 'LOOP iterate_asteroids line 4 Iteration 3 of 8'
findings.finding: Four typographic treatments in one ~20px line: 'LOOP' and 'iterate_asteroids' in ~13px mono at mid grey, 'line 4' as an underlined blue proportional link at a smaller size, then 'Iteration 3 of 8' in mono at a visibly larger size and darker weight. The largest, darkest text in the strip is the ordinal, so the iteration counter outranks the loop it counts; and the underlined sans link is set inside a mono run, which breaks the line's baseline texture mid-phrase.

findings.location: Code pane, bottom edge — line 54, y≈1071–1075

A row-height-aligned clip, or the same fade applied vertically, would remove the sliced glyphs.

findings.location: identity bar hash vs Transaction pane header hash vs Transaction pane FEE PAYER and TARGET rows

The identity bar uses 0xb63616…6359 (6 lead, 4 tail); the Transaction pane header uses 0xb636167a…66d46359 (8 lead, 8 tail) directly above the same hash printed in full; FEE PAYER and TARGET are printed in full and hard-wrapped mid-string onto a right-aligned second line, stranding 'e430d5d932' and 'a59161624c' as orphan fragments with no ellipsis, no continuation marker and no byte boundary. A reader cannot tell the second line continues the first rather than being a second field.

findings.location: call trace column-header row, 'FRAME' and 'ACIR opcodes'
findings.finding: Two headers of identical rank in one row, set two ways: FRAME is letterspaced uppercase sans, while 'ACIR opcodes' is a mono uppercase acronym followed by a lowercase proportional word. Neither reads as the same object as the other.

findings.location: Transaction pane, EXECUTIONS section — 'private' and 'public' sub-labels

The sub-labels therefore read as values rather than as labels for the pills beside them.

findings.location: Values pane, right-hand type column
findings.finding: Field, u32 and [Field; 8] are Noir type identifiers set in the UI proportional face while the name and value columns beside them are mono. The type column inverts it.

findings.location: Values pane 'masses[2]' row; call trace indentation guide

findings.location: call trace, current frame row 6 ('calculate_damage · 63') versus row 3

findings.location: identity bar, between 'Engine loading — 18 MB' and the position readout '128 / 1315'
findings.finding: Two unrelated quantities abut in the same dark grey with roughly a word-and-a-half of space between them. findings.location: middle column, Call Trace / Event Log tabbed region, y 500–740
findings.finding: The tabbed region runs y248–741 (492px, 60% of the 826px pane column) but its content — tab strip, FRAME header, seven frames, footer — ends at y=499. 240px, 49% of the region, is empty white below the 'By call order. / Self cost' footer, and the footer is not pinned to the pane floor, so it reads as a row of the frame list with a void beneath it. The shell's outer margins are four different values. There is a 24px band of bare page background above the provenance banner (y0–23, no border, no content), the banner card is full-bleed x0–1919, the pane column insets 4px on both sides (borders at x=4 and x=1915), and the bottom margin is 4px (border y=1075). The 24px top band is dead space in the register where rows are scarcest.

findings.location: provenance banner, y 24–179
findings.finding: The banner costs 156px plus the 24px above it — 180px, 17% of the viewport — and uses 31% of its own width: badge at x10–166 and four prose lines from x=11 to a maximum of x=602, leaving 1300px of empty card to the right. findings.location: identity bar vs pane column, left and right edges

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, label column, rows BLOCK / CANONICAL / FINALITY / FEE PAYER / TARGET / COST·MANA
findings.finding: Labels are top-aligned to their values, not baseline-aligned. Measured cap-tops: BLOCK 380 vs 383, CANONICAL 410 vs 413, FINALITY 441 vs 444, FEE PAYER 473 vs 476, TARGET 524 vs 527, COST·MANA 575 vs 577 — the label sits 3px high in every row, and because the label is set smaller its baseline lands ~4px above the value's. findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, identity rows y 276–330 and FEE PAYER / TARGET rows y 465–566

findings.location: Code pane header stack, file-tab row y 313–340
findings.finding: Four stacked header rows in one pane use three left edges: 'CODE' at x=13, 'LOOP iterate_asteroids …' at x=14, the file tabs 'Nargo.toml Prover.toml src/main.nr src/shield.nr' at x=22, and the 'Showing from line 26 —' notice at x=13. findings.location: Code pane gutter (y 462–484 and y 532–554) and Values pane rows 'remaining_shield' / 'damage' (x 922)

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail, active FETCHING segment, x 1229–1233

The fill (219,234,254) starts cleanly at x=1232; only the accent fails to follow the radius.

findings.location: the three pane header strips, y 248–275
findings.finding: Header strips are not the same height: Code 248–273 and Transaction 248–273 (25px), but the Call Trace / Event Log tab strip is 248–275 (27px) because the active-tab underline sits at y271–273, 2px above the strip's own bottom border.
