findings.location: Code pane, bottom edge y 1064–1075
findings.finding: Line 54 is bisected horizontally by the pane's bottom border with zero bottom padding — roughly half a glyph height is visible and unreadable. The same pane handles horizontal overflow well (lines 40 and 53 dissolve into a soft fade at the right edge), so the two axes of one pane get two different overflow treatments. A few px of bottom padding, or the same fade applied vertically, would make the cut deliberate.

findings.location: identity bar, y 197–224
findings.finding: The bar reads as grouped rather than as a strip of unrelated objects — identity, divider at x=345, then four control pills at an even 16px pitch, scrubber, readout, phase rail, and two right-anchored actions after a 326px gap — and every object is centred on y=210.5 exactly. Working against that are four object heights in one 28px band: stepping groups 28px, share/download buttons 26px, Partial badge and phase rail 22px, scrubber track 16px. Two interactive button families 2px apart in height is the one that shows.

findings.location: Code pane inline chip on line 32 (`damage: 0→2000`) versus Values pane rows `remaining_shield 9000` and `damage 2000`; and the `Partial` chip in the identity bar and at the top of the Transaction pane
findings.finding: One state, "this value changed at the current step", is drawn in two different hues in two panes the eye crosses between constantly: a green outlined chip in Code, amber text with an amber left rule in Values. Worse, that amber is the same amber as the `Partial` trace-status chip, so amber means both "changed here" and "this trace is incomplete" on one screen — and amber is also the code palette's numeric-literal colour forty pixels away (`100`, `1`, `90`). A reader cannot learn a rule from this. Pick one hue for delta and take it out of the status vocabulary.

findings.location: Whole shell — the seam between the VALUES pane and the CALL TRACE pane above it, the CODE pane's left edge against the page background, and the provenance banner's boundary with the identity bar
findings.finding: Page background, pane header bands, pane bodies and the provenance banner all sit within a few percent lightness of white, so surface level carries no information and every pane boundary depends on a single hairline — the exact failing example named in B4. This is the strongest evidence the light theme is inherited by inversion: an elevation step that is clearly visible as a lift on near-black falls below the perceptual threshold when applied as a drop on near-white. The register's own reference (the desktop app) separates panes by surface, not by rule. Light needs its own, larger, step sizes rather than the dark ramp reflected.

findings.location: Code pane current line (line 32) and Call Trace selected row (`calculate_damage`) — both cyan; versus the loop strip's "Iteration 3 of 8" selector where box 3 is a dark grey fill
findings.finding: "Current position" is expressed by a saturated cyan fill in two panes and by a neutral dark-grey fill in the loop-iteration strip, which is also a position readout and sits inside the same pane as one of the cyan marks. Two colours for one role. The cyan itself is off the page's accent family (everything else interactive is blue/indigo) and has the flat, high-chroma pastel quality of a dark-theme selection colour lightened for white — it is the only place this hue appears. Either promote cyan to the single position role and apply it to the iteration selector, or restate position in the accent family.

findings.location: Identity bar, stepping control cluster between the exit/hash group and the scrubber — the four button groups spanning roughly x370–x660
findings.finding: The four stepping groups render at two clearly different ink levels on an identical white surface, with no other differentiator: no fill change, no border change, no reduced opacity on the container. Because the engine is still loading (`FETCHING`), the reader's live question is which controls are disabled, and the answer is unreadable — a lighter glyph on white reads as a lighter icon weight, not as unavailable. Dimming is a dark-theme disabled idiom that does not survive the flip; light needs a disabled treatment that changes more than ink density.

findings.location: Identity bar — scrubber/meter fill, the `FETCHING` chip and its `OPENING` / `POSITIONING` neighbours, and the link-coloured `← aztec` exit, `line 4`, `Self cost` and `101:0`
findings.finding: Three distinct blue-family hue angles sit within 900px of one bar: a dark cyan-slate meter fill, a mid-blue chip on a pale blue wash, and an indigo used for links. Brief §2 makes the accent hue family the thing shared across registers; three angles is not a family, it is three accents. The practical damage is that the `FETCHING` chip is chromatically indistinguishable in role from the link-blue actions beside it, so a live engine phase reads as a clickable badge, while the provenance badge at the top of the page uses the same pale-blue-on-blue treatment for a third meaning again.

findings.location: Identity bar phase rail — `OPENING` and `POSITIONING` to the right of the `FETCHING` chip
findings.finding: The two not-yet-reached phase labels are simultaneously the smallest and the lowest-contrast text on the page: uppercase, tracked, roughly 11px, in a light grey on white. B2 explicitly declines to reward density bought at the cost of contrast. The rail is the honest substitute for a progress percentage, so the phases it has not reached still have to be readable for the reader to know what is coming.

findings.location: Code pane header stack — the `CODE` title row, the file-tab row (`Nargo.toml` … `src/shield.nr`) and the "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below…" notice
findings.finding: Three stacked bands share one surface tint and one grey text level, so an informational notice about the window is styled identically to structural pane chrome and the whole stack reads as a single three-row header. The notice is content and should sit on the pane body surface, or carry an informational tint, so the reader can tell chrome from message.

findings.location: Transaction pane — the `Yes` (CANONICAL) and `Safe` (FINALITY) chips versus the `Not observable` chip in the EXECUTIONS block
findings.finding: The same neutral grey chip carries two opposite kinds of statement: affirmed facts about the transaction, and the absence of observable data. The adjacent green `Trace ready` shows the palette does have a positive tone available, so the greys read as unstyled defaults rather than a chosen neutral role. Distinguishing a fact chip from a not-available chip would let the right column be scanned by colour.

findings.location: navigation column, Call Trace region (y 245-740) vs Values pane (y 745-1080)
findings.finding: The call-trace region is 495px tall; the last frame ends at y 480 and the 'By call order. / Self cost' footer at y 505, leaving 235px — 47% of the region — empty. The Values pane below it fits eleven rows with ~45px of slack, while the Code pane is cut mid-glyph at line 54 and the Transaction pane's RAW JSON is cut mid-object at "transfer". The answer to the open measurement is that the Values pane should have the height: a real Noir frame has dozens of locals and this fixture already fills eleven rows, whereas seven frames fill barely half the region they are given. Make the tabbed region shrink toward its content and let Values take the remainder.

findings.location: provenance banner, y 0-178
findings.finding: The banner takes 178px, 16.5% of the 1080px viewport and about seven code rows or seven call-trace frames, before the identity bar begins. Its cost is not the content but the layout: four lines of prose set at a ~580px measure inside a 1904px band, so roughly 1330x130px of the band is blank. The same sentences at a 1100-1200px measure are two lines, and badge + slug + two lines lands near 110px, returning ~60px to the pane column that is currently clipping two panes.

findings.location: Transaction pane, DECODED INPUT block (SELECTOR and RAW rows, y ~775-810)
findings.finding: SELECTOR and RAW both render as a bare `0x` with no bytes after the prefix, and the three lines of prose immediately below assert that "the parameters are shown as raw bytes". No bytes are shown. Five rows of the register's scarcest resource carry zero information, and the copy describes a state the rows do not contain. If there is genuinely no calldata, the honest row is a named absence, not a prefix.

findings.location: Transaction pane, FEE PAYER (y ~480-505) and TARGET (y ~530-555)
findings.finding: Both 20-byte values wrap onto a second, right-ragged line broken at an arbitrary character (…e2a272b5 / e430d5d932). Each costs two rows in the pane whose bottom content is already clipped, and a two-line ragged block is materially harder to compare against another address than a single line. The same data type is middle-ellipsis-truncated in the identity bar (0xb63616…6359) and in this pane's own header (0xb636167a…66d46359), so one screen carries two treatments and the expensive one is the less legible.

findings.location: Code pane, lines 40 and 53 at the pane's right edge (x ~910)
findings.finding: Long signatures are hard-cut mid-token — "shield_regen_perce" on line 40, "damage: Field, r" on line 53 — with no ellipsis, no fade and no visible overflow affordance, so the reader cannot tell whether more parameters exist. The Transaction pane's RAW block on the same screen does apply a right-edge fade to its overflowing hex, so the product already has a treatment for this and the Code pane is not using it.

findings.location: Code pane header stack, y 245-385 (pane title, LOOP/iteration row, file tabs, prose row)
findings.finding: Four bands and ~140px — 17% of the pane's 835px, about six code lines — sit above the first code line in a pane whose content is cut mid-line at the viewport bottom. The worst offender is the full-width sentence "Showing from line 26 — the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.", which restates what the line-number gutter already states and is the only band of the four carrying no navigation. Folding it into the gutter or the pane title returns a code line and removes a paragraph from a register that admits exactly one prose band.

findings.location: identity bar, stepping controls x 372-660 and the empty span x 1478-1800
findings.finding: Eight icon-only buttons in four visually identical pairs, each a ~14px arrow glyph in a ~28px button, with no labels and no keyboard hints — at a glance step-over, step-into, frame boundary and run-to-end are indistinguishable. Meanwhile 322px of the bar between the phase rail and the NOIR tag is empty. That empty span is the budget the differentiation needs; B10's "keyboard affordances are indicated" is the only part of the criterion this bar misses, and it misses it while holding the space to fix it.

findings.location: Transaction pane, y ~283-320 (hash header and the line below it)
findings.finding: The transaction hash appears twice on consecutive rows — `0xb636167a…66d46359` truncated beside the Partial badge, then the full 42-character value on the row immediately below. One row of the pane is spent restating the row above it, in the pane whose RAW block is clipped by the viewport bottom. Keep the full value and drop the truncation from the header row, or vice versa.

findings.location: Code pane, code rows y 385-1080
findings.finding: Code rows run ~23px at roughly 13px mono, a 1.75 line-height that is loose for this register; 29 lines fill ~695px where ~19px rows would show 36. This is partly earned — the inline value chips (`damage: 0→2000`, `shield_pct=90`) need vertical room and the overflow chips at lines 26 and 48 already take half-rows of their own — so it is a tension rather than a clean loss, but the rows without chips do not need the leading.

findings.location: provenance banner, y 22-178, full width
findings.finding: The banner is drawn in the explorer/docs register, not the tool register: a floating rounded card with a blue left-accent rail and hairline border, inset on the page canvas with a 22px top margin, its body set in the explorer's geometric sans at body size with generous leading. Every other surface in this shell is a flush pane on a grey title band. Its longest line ends at x=605 inside a card that runs to x=1912, so ~68% of the full-width band it insists on is empty, and it spends 178px (16.5%) of a 1080 viewport before the tool begins. The content is right and belongs here; the drawing is borrowed. A two-line tool-chrome strip carrying the same sentences would return roughly 100px to the panes.

findings.location: Call Trace / Event Log tab strip (x 930, y 261) versus CODE (x 16, y 261), VALUES (x 932, y 759) and TRANSACTION (x 1542, y 261)
findings.finding: The pane-title primitive is not one primitive. CODE, VALUES and TRANSACTION are set in the uppercase monospace that is this product's chrome texture; CALL TRACE and EVENT LOG are set in a letterspaced sans, as is the FRAME column header directly beneath them. Four panes, two title faces, and the odd one out is precisely the region this milestone just restructured into tabs — so the change reads as bolted on rather than native. The same split recurs inside one row: FRAME (sans) and ACIR opcodes (mono) at x 1425, y 292.

findings.location: banner badge (x 8-165, y 44) and phase rail (x 1225-1470, y 203) versus the Partial / Yes / Safe / Not observable / Trace ready chips in the identity bar and TRANSACTION pane
findings.finding: The status-chip primitive splits in two. The banner badge and the phase rail are fully-rounded pills; every other status chip on the screen is a ~5px-radius rounded rectangle with a tinted fill and matching border. The banner badge is additionally the only English-phrase chip set in monospace, while Not observable and Trace ready are sans. The register's single most load-bearing label — the one that tells the reader this chain is synthetic — is drawn in a badge vocabulary used nowhere else on the surface, which reads as a component from another page rather than a deliberate emphasis.

findings.location: identity bar status region, x 950-1470, y 211
findings.finding: The copy contradicts the surface it sits on. 'Engine loading - 18 MB' with FETCHING lit on the phase rail sits inches from a position readout of 128 / 1315, above four panes that are fully populated and pinned at line 32 with values resolved. Both statements are presumably true of a statically rendered session with the engine still hydrating, but the bar never says so, so one half of it announces a state the other half has already left. In a product that treats honesty as a design property, two adjacent readouts describing different states is the copy problem to fix first: qualify the status ('positioned - engine hydrating, 18 MB') rather than leaving the reader to reconcile them.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, label column x 1542, y 253-920
findings.finding: Three semantic levels reuse one label primitive. The pane title TRANSACTION, the section headings EXECUTIONS / DECODED INPUT / RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE), and the field labels BLOCK / CANONICAL / FINALITY / FEE PAYER / TARGET / COST-MANA / SELECTOR / RAW are all the same uppercase monospace at the same size, weight and grey. Only the title's grey fill band separates chrome from data; the section headings get nothing, so scanning the column FINALITY and EXECUTIONS read as peers when one is a field and one opens a section. The desktop app distinguishes chrome labels from data labels; here the distinction is carried entirely by a background fill.

Two link treatments coexist. The three in-pane targets are blue and underlined - the explorer's document-link affordance - while the exit from the register, the one genuine navigation on the page, is blue and not underlined. 'Self cost' is worse placed than the others: it is a pane control sitting in the call trace's footer strip dressed as body-copy hyperlink. Invert the emphasis so the register exit is the thing that looks like a link and in-pane targets use a tool affordance.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, 'Status reason: private-part-succeeded-public-part-succeeded', y 347-370
findings.finding: The only item in that column set as a running sentence in the sans body face rather than in the pane's label/value grid, and its value is a raw kebab-case enum printed verbatim across two wrapped lines. It is neither the machine token (which would sit in mono in the grid under a STATUS REASON label) nor English prose. Pick one; as drawn it breaks the column's rhythm to deliver a slug.

findings.location: Code pane notice strip, y 358
findings.finding: 'Showing from line 26 - the session's position is below, and the lines above it are not in this window.' is honest and worth keeping, but it is fourteen words of conversational prose in a register that states itself elsewhere in three ('By call order.', 'ACIR opcodes'). The desktop-app voice for this is nearer 'window starts at line 26'; the current phrasing carries the explorer's explanatory tone into a tool pane.

findings.location: Transaction pane (right rail), the COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row, between FINALITY and EXECUTIONS
findings.finding: The dangling " / " is fixed; the unit now reads cleanly as `mana (FeeJuice)`. Three defects remain, and together they still make this the weakest element on the page. (a) The fee is a 32-byte word printed raw — `0x` followed by 64 nibbles of which roughly 46 are literal zero padding, with the only significant part, `185cfcc84d2f103f`, stranded at the end. It is a quantity a reader cannot read, compare, or sanity-check, on the one view whose purpose is to show that real chain data survives the formatting path the fixture never reaches. (b) It wraps across three right-aligned lines plus a fourth for the unit, so the row stands about four times the height of BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY and its value block overruns leftward under the label on the first two lines — the label/value column relationship that holds for every other row in the pane collapses here, and it collapses in the pane's most valuable vertical space, which this register already spends on a full-width banner. (c) The label is still the adapter's raw camelCase field `transactionFee`, uppercased into the unbroken token `TRANSACTIONFEE`, sitting beside BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY, EXECUTIONS and DECODED INPUT — every one of which is real English. It is a vocabulary leak from the data layer straight onto the surface. Nothing else on this page is broken: the empty panes are empty by necessity and each says why in its own voice, and the telemetry is intact. This row is the single place where the product looks like it polished the fixture and left real data raw — which is precisely the impression this capture exists to refute.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row (approx x1540-1910, y480-548)
findings.finding: The fee is rendered as a full 66-character raw hex quantity in mono, right-aligned, wrapping onto three lines at arbitrary character offsets, with the unit 'mana (FeeJuice)' on a fourth line in the proportional face. Every other row in this pane (BLOCK, CANONICAL, FINALITY) is a single-line label/value pair, so this row is four times the height of its neighbours and its label sits alone opposite a block of digits. The 47 leading zeros dominate and the only meaningful digits (185cfcc84d2f103f) land on the last line, so the value cannot be read at a glance or compared to anything. Format it as a decimal mana figure, or apply the same middle-ellipsis truncation the page already uses for hashes (0x0000…f103f) and keep the full value on copy/hover, so the row returns to one line and one type level.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane label column, EXECUTIONS (y568) and DECODED INPUT (y619) versus BLOCK (y386), CANONICAL (y416), FINALITY (y448), SELECTOR (y643), RAW (y668), RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) (y771)
findings.finding: Section headings and field labels are set in exactly the same face, size, weight, colour, letter-spacing and case. Nothing in the type says that SELECTOR and RAW are children of DECODED INPUT while BLOCK is a peer field, so the pane reads as one flat list of eleven identical labels and the reader must parse the values to recover the structure. Introduce one step of separation: either raise section headings a size and weight, or drop field labels to a lighter secondary level, and indent the rows that belong to a section.

findings.location: provenance banner prose (x14-610, y78-182) relative to the identity-bar hash '0x0858d6…7fb2' (x143, y233)
findings.finding: The banner's five-line paragraph is set at the same body size as pane content and is by a wide margin the largest and longest run of text on the page, while the session's subject — the transaction hash — is a single string on the identity bar at roughly the same size and no greater weight. Read without reading, the page announces itself as a paragraph of provenance chrome rather than as a debugging session over a specific transaction. Give the banner prose a distinct secondary level (one step down in size, or a lighter weight, kept above the legibility floor) and give the identity-bar hash a step up, so the top two bands read as annotation and subject rather than as two equals.

findings.location: CODE pane paragraph (x20-605, y322-448), CALL TRACE pane (x930-1500, y315-353), VALUES pane (x930-1508, y796-833)
findings.finding: The three limitation explanations are set at the same size, weight and colour as each other and as the banner prose, so the type scale has no level for a pane state message. In a pane roughly 780px tall holding two sentences flush to its top edge, that gives the reader no typographic signal that the emptiness is deliberate rather than content that failed to render. The CODE pane compounds it: 'Stepping continues at instruction level.' is a second paragraph identical in every type attribute to the explanation whose last clause already said 'Stepping is complete', so it reads as a stray repeat rather than a live status line. Add a state-message level (secondary colour or a size step, optionally with a small caps label) and set the status line at a different level from the explanation.

findings.location: identity bar hash (x143, y233) versus TRANSACTION pane header hash (x1642, y312) and the full hash beneath it (x1540-1908, y330-368)
findings.finding: Two truncation shapes for the same value are on screen at once: 6+4 ('0x0858d6…7fb2') on the identity bar and 8+8 ('0x0858d644…22e67fb2') in the pane header. Directly below, the full 64-character hash wraps after character 41, splitting a byte ('…430aabc0' / '6ef9ace…'), so the two lines cannot be scanned as byte groups. Standardise on one truncation shape across the view and break the full hash on byte boundaries or in fixed 8- or 16-character groups.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, DECODED INPUT section, RAW row value (x1890, y671)
findings.finding: The value renders as a bare '0x' with no digits after it, right-aligned against the pane edge in the same mono treatment used for truncated values elsewhere on the page. Typographically it reads as a value that has been clipped, not as an empty calldata payload. Distinguish it from a truncation — '0x (empty)', or the em-dash used for absent values — so the type does not imply missing characters.

findings.location: three-column pane split: CODE pane (x4-917, y269-1075), CALL TRACE (x922-1527, y269-750), VALUES (x922-1527, y757-1075), TRANSACTION (x1532-1915, y269-1075)
findings.finding: The split allocates 1523px of width to eight lines of prose and 383px to everything the session actually knows. The CODE pane is a 913x806 region holding four lines and one button, roughly 93 percent empty; CALL TRACE holds two lines in 605x481; VALUES holds two lines in 605x313. Meanwhile the TRANSACTION pane is the only pane with data and is the only one that runs out of room: its RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block reaches the pane's bottom border at y1075 with the JSON object still unclosed, and its fee value wraps three times purely because the column is narrow. This is the starved-pane-beside-an-empty-pane case in B4. For a session with no source, either widen the right column (a 560-620px TRANSACTION column would end the fee wrap and show the rest of the replay object) or let the empty CODE pane yield width, so the split responds to what this trace actually contains.

findings.location: provenance banner card (x4-1918, y20-200); its prose occupies only x11-610
findings.finding: The banner is 180px tall plus a 20px margin above it — 200 of 1080 rows, 19 percent of the viewport — and its paragraph is set to a roughly 600px measure inside a 1912px card, so x610-1910 (68 percent of the band) is empty. It pays full-width cost for third-width content, and those rows come straight out of the panes in the one register where vertical space is the scarcest resource. Reflow the sentences across the available width, or set the badge and slug in a left column with the prose in one or two columns beside them: at a 1200px measure the same text is two or three lines instead of six and returns roughly 90-100px to the pane grid without dropping a word of provenance.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row (label at x1541 y480; value block x1712-1907, y476-532)
findings.finding: The raw 66-character hex fee wraps into three right-aligned lines plus a fourth line for 'mana (FeeJuice)', making this row about 72px tall against 30px for BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY directly above it. The label sits alone on the first of four lines, so the label/value pairing that governs every other row in the pane is lost, and because the block is right-aligned its left edge is ragged (lines 1-2 begin at x1712, line 3 at x1766) — the eye has no column to follow. The wrap points fall mid-byte. Fix the row rather than the string: give the value a fixed left-aligned column and wrap on byte or 16-character boundaries, or middle-truncate as the hashes already do, so the row returns to the pane's single-line rhythm.

findings.location: left margin of the shell, top to bottom: banner body text x11, CODE pane header label x14, CODE pane body text x20, identity-bar back-link '← aztec-testnet' x23
findings.finding: Four different left edges within 12px of each other and none of them shared, so scanning down the left side of the page nothing lines up. The stagger has three separate causes: the banner card uses about 7px of inner padding where the pane cards use 15px for body content; the identity bar is not a card and carries its own 23px inset; and within a single pane the header label (x14) and the body text it heads (x20) are 6px apart, which is a misalignment inside one component. Pick one content edge for the shell — the pane body edge at x20 is the natural one since it governs the largest area — and set the banner padding, the identity-bar inset and the pane header label to it.

findings.location: identity bar, phase rail, active FETCHING segment (container x1313-1571, y221-245; artifact at x1313-1317)
findings.finding: The active segment's blue fill is inset from the container's pill border and its corner radius does not match the container's, so at the rail's left end a 2px dark-blue arc sits outside the fill, separated from it by a white sliver. At 100 percent this reads as an opening parenthesis before the word FETCHING — a layout artifact that scans as a text character in the page's primary state indicator. Clip the active fill to the container (inherit the pill radius on the first and last segments, or apply overflow clipping on the rail) so the highlight meets the border with no gap.

findings.location: CODE pane (content ends y511, pane ends y1075), CALL TRACE (content ends y353, pane ends y750), VALUES (content ends y833, pane ends y1075)
findings.finding: Asked whether the empty regions read as deliberate: yes, but only just. Each pane is framed and titled, so none reads as a failed render, and the emptiness itself is correct. What is weak is the composition — all three place their explanation flush to the pane's top-left and leave 397px, 397px and 242px of unanchored space below it, so the eye is pulled to the top-left corner of a large void three times. Anchoring each explanation as a bounded notice block (a bordered or tinted card at a fixed measure, optionally centred in the pane's upper third) would make the empty area read as a designed state rather than as content that stopped early, without showing one word less.

findings.location: identity bar, stepping-control cluster (x473-758, y221-245): four button pairs at x473-530, x546-598, x616-678, x696-758
findings.finding: The four control groups have three different widths (57, 52, 62 and 62px) because each button is sized to its glyph rather than to a fixed control size; individual buttons run 26 to 32px, a 23 percent spread across eight buttons of the same class. The gaps between groups are consistent at 16-18px, so the irregularity reads as the buttons themselves being uneven. Set one fixed min-width for the icon buttons so the cluster has a single horizontal rhythm.

findings.location: CODE pane, 'Supply sources' button (left border x13.7, y488-511) versus the prose above it (x20.8)
findings.finding: The button's left edge sits about 7px left of the paragraph it answers; it happens to line up with the pane header label at x14 instead. Since it is the pane's only interactive element and its whole job is to be the route out of the limitation the prose describes, it should share that prose's left edge. Align the button to the pane body edge.

findings.location: shell outer margins: 20px of page background above the banner card (y0-20) versus 4px at the left and right edges and 5px column gutters
findings.finding: The outer margin is 20px on top and 4px on the sides, and the internal gutters are 5px, so the shell's own frame uses three values that are not on one scale. In a register that fits its whole layout into 1080px the 20px band above the banner is also the most expensive of the three. Bring the top margin onto the same step as the side margins and gutters.

findings.location: whole shell, concentrated on the identity bar (y 213-263)
findings.finding: The light theme is a default palette, not a designed counterpart to the CodeTracer dark surface. Every neutral is exactly achromatic (#101010, #242424, #484848, #565656, #919191, #A2A2A2, #C8C8C8, #DDDDDD, #F3F3F3, #ECECEB) while every accent is an unmodified stock value drawn from four unrelated hue families: indigo-600 #4F46E5 (exit link, BLOCK value), blue-600 #2563EB / blue-100 #DBEAFE / blue-800 #1E40AF (phase rail), cyan-800 #155E75 (progress fill), green-600 #16A34A / green-100 #DCFCE7 / green-800 #166534 (chips). Nothing carries a shared hue cast, so the theme reads as framework defaults over a gray ramp. Pick one accent family for the product, derive the rest from it, and give the neutrals a slight cast that ties the light theme to the dark one.

findings.location: provenance banner (y 20-200), identity bar (y 201-263), and all four pane bodies
findings.finding: There is no elevation system: the provenance banner, the identity bar and every pane body are all #FFFFFF, and the banner and identity bar are divided only by a bare #A2A2A2 hairline at y=200 with no gutter, so the register's only provenance marker is fused to the command bar. The two other surface values invert the model rather than extend it: the pane header band is #DDDDDD, darker than the #ECECEB page canvas it sits on, and the RAW (chain-native) code block in the transaction pane reuses #ECECEB exactly, so the innermost inset surface equals the outermost canvas and the pane bottom edge (y 1075) reads as a hole rather than a raised edge. Define three distinct surface levels (canvas, pane, inset) and put the banner and the identity bar on different ones.

findings.location: identity bar: progress bar (x 775-1035) and phase rail (x 1320-1570)
findings.finding: One engine-loading state is expressed in two unrelated accent families 300px apart on the same bar: the determinate progress fill is cyan-800 #155E75 while the phase rail marks the active FETCHING phase with a blue-100 #DBEAFE fill, blue-800 #1E40AF text and a blue-600 #2563EB left bar. Worse, that blue-600 accent bar sits within 30 degrees of hue of the indigo-600 #4F46E5 used for navigable links on the same bar, so two near-identical blues carry different meanings (active phase vs. link) side by side. Render the progress fill in the same accent as the active phase chip, and keep the link hue clearly separated from it.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane: full hash (y 332-370) vs. COST TRANSACTIONFEE value (y 475-535) vs. identity bar hash (x 140-255)
findings.finding: Text emphasis is allocated against importance. The same data type (monospace hex) appears at three ink levels: the truncated hash on the identity bar is #101010, the raw fee quantity and the RAW JSON are #242424, and the full transaction hash - the transaction pane's identity line - is #484848, the same ink as ordinary body prose in the Code and Values panes. The least meaningful value on the page, an undecoded 32-byte fee blob wrapping three lines, therefore carries more emphasis than the identity it belongs to, and its ink gives no signal that it is raw rather than formatted (only the #484848 'mana (FeeJuice)' unit says so). Promote the full hash to the primary ink level and demote the undecoded fee to the same de-emphasised level as other raw byte values.

findings.location: stepping controls (x 470-760, y 218-248) vs. 'Supply sources' button (x 12-122, y 488-512)
findings.finding: One button primitive has two colour treatments, and the register's primary controls are the fainter of the two. The eight stepping buttons use a #C8C8C8 border on white - 1.67:1, below the 3:1 non-text floor - with #565656 glyphs, so the group reads as ghost outlines; the 'Supply sources' button uses a #A2A2A2 border (2.55:1) with a #101010 label. Neither reaches 3:1, and there is no role difference to justify the divergence. Unify the button border and label tokens and raise the border to at least 3:1 against #FFFFFF.

findings.location: 'Real Aztec testnet data' badge (x 6-186, y 42-65), 'Succeeded' chips on the identity bar and in the TRANSACTION pane, 'Trace ready' chip (y 580-602)
findings.finding: The green chip role carries three different kinds of statement in identical clothing - fill #DCFCE7, border #16A34A, text #166534 in all four instances. 'Real Aztec testnet data' is a provenance claim about where the data came from, 'Succeeded' is a fact the chain reported, and 'Trace ready' is a claim about a product artefact. In the register the brief flags as the one where a reader is most likely to confuse a product claim with a chain fact, the colour system says all three are the same kind of assertion. Also, the #16A34A border sits at exactly 3.00:1 on its own #DCFCE7 fill. Give provenance its own chip role, distinct from chain-reported status.

findings.location: identity bar progress bar, boundary at x=868 (y 228-238)
findings.finding: Inside the progress bar the cyan-800 #155E75 fill and the #919191 track differ by only 2.31:1, so the one boundary the component exists to show is the weakest edge on the identity bar; the #919191 track is also the heaviest neutral on that bar, darker than the #DDDDDD pane headers, so the unfilled remainder reads as filled. The adjacent '128 / 345' readout carries the same information in text, so nothing is lost today. Lighten the track to a #DDDDDD-class neutral so the fill boundary clears 3:1.

findings.location: CODE pane, x 6-916 / y 270-1075
findings.finding: The trace has 345 recorded instruction indices and is positioned at 128, but the pane displays none of them: four lines of prose, one redundant restatement ('Stepping continues at instruction level.'), a button, and 555px of blank below it. The pane's own copy says stepping is complete and only the text is missing, so render the program-counter stream as rows (index, PC, and where known opcode) with 128 highlighted. That turns the register's largest surface from an apology into the instruction listing it is describing.

findings.location: three-pane split: CODE (910px), CALL TRACE/VALUES (606px), TRANSACTION (380px)
findings.finding: Space is allocated inversely to content. The 1516px left two thirds carry nine lines of prose across roughly 1.2 megapixels, while the 380px TRANSACTION pane holds every fact on the page and pays for it: the fee wraps over three lines and the RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) block is cut off at the pane's bottom edge mid-object. At 1920 the additional width over a 1280 layout goes entirely into empty panes. Widen the TRANSACTION column at this breakpoint, or promote the replay telemetry into the empty left region.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row, y 468-548
findings.finding: The fee renders as an unformatted 32-byte hex quantity wrapped over three right-aligned lines plus a fourth line for 'mana (FeeJuice)', making the row ~80px tall against ~32px for BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY and destroying the single-line label/value grid those rows establish. The wraps also fall mid-byte. Render the decoded mana figure with tabular digits on one line and keep the raw hex as a secondary or copy-on-demand value; if it must stay raw, elide the 58 leading zeros rather than wrapping them.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, DECODED INPUT block, SELECTOR and RAW rows, y 618-680
findings.finding: SELECTOR renders as a bare en-dash and RAW renders as a bare '0x' with no bytes after the prefix, directly above prose stating that 'the parameters are shown as raw bytes'. No bytes are shown, so a prefix with no operand reads as a truncated render rather than an empty value, and the sentence below contradicts what is on screen. Either print the raw calldata bytes, or replace both values with an explicit 'none recorded' and reword the sentence to match.

findings.location: identity bar, progress bar x 778-1035 and position readout x 1220-1300
findings.finding: The widest horizontal element on the identity bar is a partly filled bar that encodes engine bytes downloaded, not trace position, and it sits in the same control group as the 128 / 345 readout, where a debugger user reads a long horizontal bar as a timeline scrubber. The actual position has no graphical representation in any pane. Move the download bar away from the position cluster (or reduce it to a compact spinner beside its label) and give 128 / 345 the scrubber treatment.

findings.location: CALL TRACE pane, x 921-1527 / y 270-748
findings.finding: The pane states that frames are recorded but never says how many, and shows none of them, leaving ~400px blank. Frame count, depth and PC range are data this recording has even without symbols; listing anonymous frames as 'frame 0 · depth 0 · pc 12-97' rows would make the pane scannable and would quantify the claim it currently only asserts.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane header, y 300-370
findings.finding: The transaction hash appears three times in the top 160px of the page: truncated beside the Succeeded badge, in full wrapped over two lines immediately below, and again truncated on the identity bar. In the narrowest and most content-starved pane on the page this costs three rows for one value. Drop the truncated copy in the pane and keep the full hash only.

findings.location: identity bar, stepping control cluster x 470-770
findings.finding: Eight unlabelled glyphs of roughly 11px sit in four groups, and three pairs are hard to discriminate at that size: the two bracketed arrows, the two double-chevrons and the two diagonal arrows all read as 'jump to an end'. There is ~380px of unused bar between the phase rail and the share/download icons at this viewport; spend some of it on keyboard hints or short labels rather than leaving it empty.

findings.location: the no-source explanations in the CODE, CALL TRACE and VALUES panes (CALL TRACE body, x approx. 930-1500, y approx. 320-350, above roughly 700px of empty pane)
findings.finding: The explanations are set as explorer-register body prose — proportional sans at roughly the same size as marketing copy, a 570px measure, paragraph spacing — floated at the top-left of otherwise empty panes with no empty-state treatment at all. Nothing distinguishes a pane that is correctly empty from one that failed to render: no muted surface, no framing, no centring, no icon, no rule under the note. The desktop app would set this as a small muted pane note, not as an article. Give the three notes one shared empty-state component: reduced size, muted foreground, vertically placed within the pane rather than pinned to its top edge, so the emptiness reads as a decision.

findings.location: provenance banner, full width above the identity bar (y approx. 10-205)
findings.finding: The banner is imported into the debugger shell in explorer dress: a rounded card on a light canvas, generous internal padding, and a roughly 600px prose measure inside a 1900px band, so it spends about 20% of the viewport's rows while leaving two-thirds of its own width empty. In the one register where rows are the scarcest resource, that is the register crossing being made at the top of the page by the explorer. Keep the content verbatim, but re-dress it for this register — set the sentences at pane-note size, run them across the available width in two columns or one long line, and drop the card chrome so it reads as a shell band rather than a marketing block.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row (x approx. 1710-1905, y approx. 480-545)
findings.finding: The fee arrives as a 32-byte hex quantity and is rendered raw: 40 leading zeros wrapping across three right-ragged lines, with `mana (FeeJuice)` stranded beneath, breaking the label/value grid that every other row in the pane holds. The same primitive is a formatted mana figure on the synthetic chain, so one product primitive renders two different ways depending only on which chain reached it, and on the real one it is unreadable as a quantity. Normalise the hex to a decimal mana value at render and keep the raw hex behind a title or a secondary line, so the row stays one line and the unit stays adjacent to its number.

findings.location: identity bar, centre — `Engine loading — 18 MB` with a part-filled bar and the FETCHING chip lit (x approx. 775-1575, y approx. 233)
findings.finding: One bar asserts two states of the same session. The phase rail says the engine is still FETCHING and has not reached OPENING or POSITIONING, while eight pixels to its right the readout claims a concrete position of 128/345, and the transaction pane says `Trace ready`. A position cannot be known before the trace is opened, so the readout is asserting a state the rail says has not happened. Suppress or dim the position readout until the rail reaches POSITIONING, or label the two so a reader can see that one describes the served session and the other the hydrating engine.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, DECODED INPUT block — the SELECTOR row (value `—`), the RAW row (value `0x`) and the sentence below them (y approx. 615-750)
findings.finding: The copy and the rows contradict each other. The sentence reads "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes", but SELECTOR shows an em-dash meaning there is no selector at all, and RAW shows a bare `0x` with no bytes after it — the same dangling-operand shape the cost row was just fixed for. The explanation promises raw bytes the pane does not contain, which is the one voice failure on a page whose copy is otherwise exact. Branch the sentence: when there is no selector and no calldata, say that this call carries no input rather than explaining an ABI miss that did not occur, and render the empty value as `—` rather than `0x`.

findings.location: whole surface at the light theme — the page canvas behind the pane grid and the white pane fills (e.g. the CODE pane, x approx. 5-915)
findings.finding: The light theme of this register looks inherited from the explorer rather than designed for the tool: the same near-white canvas, the same card-like pane fills, the same green/blue accent treatment as an explorer page, with pane boundaries carried by a single hairline. Section 3 requires the crossing into the debug route to be a deliberate, visible transition, and at this theme a visitor gets no signal that the register changed. Differentiate the debugger's light theme from the explorer's — a distinctly cooler or darker canvas behind the panes, stronger pane separators, and a tighter row rhythm — so the light theme is the same tool in daylight rather than the marketing surface with panes in it.

findings.location: CODE pane, `Supply sources` button (x approx. 14-120, y approx. 488-511)
findings.finding: This is the only route out of the page's central limitation, and it is rendered in the weakest button style available — a small light outline on a white pane, below two paragraphs, with less visual weight than the `Succeeded` badge in the identity bar. Promote it to the pane's primary affordance so the missing text plainly reads as something the visitor can supply.

findings.location: TRANSACTION pane, RAW (CHAIN-NATIVE) JSON block, bottom edge of the viewport (y approx. 1063-1080)
findings.finding: The JSON stops mid-object at `"effectsMismatched": 0,` with no closing brace and no visible scrollbar or fade, so it is indistinguishable from a truncated render — the same deliberate-versus-broken ambiguity as the empty panes. Add a persistent scroll affordance or a bottom fade on the block so the reader can see the content continues.

findings.location: Overview table, final row — the COST · TRANSACTIONFEE value cell
findings.finding: The page's only quantity is printed as a 66-character zero-padded hex word: 47 leading zeros fill the data column and push the significant digits (175c1a29c1f97278) to the far right before 'mana (FeeJuice)'. The fee's order of magnitude is unreadable, so the one row whose job is to say what this transaction cost says nothing a reader can use. The row is also the only double-height one in the table because its camelCase-flattened all-caps label wraps to two lines. A cost is a number and is being treated as an address.

findings.location: Overview table, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row, value cell
findings.finding: The fee is set as an unbroken 66-character mono run, `0x0000…(50 zeros)…175c1a29c1f97278 mana (FeeJuice)`: roughly three quarters of the glyphs are padding and the eight characters that carry the magnitude sit at the far right of a ~890 px cell, so the row cannot be read as a quantity at any glance. The page elides hashes everywhere else (title `0x1c37…0410`, breadcrumb) but applies neither elision, digit grouping nor decimal conversion to the one value that is a number. Render the amount as a formatted decimal in tabular figures with the unit after it, and keep the raw word for the Raw (chain-native) block or a title attribute.

findings.location: Overview table, label column, fourth row (`COST · TRANSACTIONFEE`)
findings.finding: Uppercasing the adapter's camelCase field name destroys its only word boundary: `transactionFee` becomes the 14-character unspaced token `TRANSACTIONFEE`, which no longer scans as two words in a tracked all-caps label. It then wraps onto a second line, making this row ~52 px tall against ~27 px for BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY, so the label column's rhythm breaks on its last row. Split the identifier on case (`COST · TRANSACTION FEE`) or map it to a display label; the label column is not wide enough to absorb an unbreakable token.

findings.location: footer, the "No account, no tracking…" disclosure paragraph
findings.finding: This paragraph is the only prose on the page with no measure cap: it runs the full ~910 px content width at ~129 characters per line, nearly double the readable maximum and half again the ~85-character measure that the provenance banner and every card body already hold to (the banner wraps at ~611 px inside the same 910 px card, so a max-width exists there and simply is not applied here). Give the disclosure the same prose max-width as the banner.

findings.location: `Not observable` card, the break between "…The published reason states why." and "The node still serves this transaction's effects…"
findings.finding: Line pitch inside a paragraph is 22 px and the pitch across the paragraph break is 25 px, so a 3 px difference is the only signal that the second block is a different voice — the published chain reason reads as a continuation of BlockTracer's framing sentence. On the one page whose entire job is to make the REASON the takeaway, the reason gets no typographic distinction at all: no extra leading, no weight change, no attribution treatment. Separate the two paragraphs by a full line, and set the quoted chain reason apart (indent, rule, or a lighter/secondary emphasis level).

findings.location: page header, `0x1c37…0410` title and the full-hash line directly beneath it
findings.finding: The largest type on the page (~35 px mono) is an abbreviation of the ~15 px line immediately below it, so the H1 carries strictly less information than its own subtitle and the two lines compete for the same role. Either promote the full hash to the title at a size that fits the column, or keep the elided title and demote the full value to a copy-on-demand affordance rather than a second full-width line of the same string.

findings.location: section headings — Events, Internal calls, State changes
findings.finding: All six section headings (Overview, Decoded input, Events, Internal calls, State changes, Raw) are one size, weight and colour, but only four are preceded by a horizontal rule; Internal calls and State changes have none. Without reading the words, those two therefore read as subordinate to Events rather than as its peers, which is exactly backwards on this view where the two trace-derived sections are the ones a reader must notice are permanently empty. Either rule every sibling heading or none.

findings.location: breadcrumb line, `Home / aztec-mainnet / tx / 0x1c37…0410`
findings.finding: The crumb mixes faces mid-line at one nominal size: `Home` is set in the sans while `aztec-mainnet`, `tx` and the elided hash are mono. The mono's smaller apparent x-height makes the first crumb read as larger than the rest, so a single-level trail looks like two levels. Set the whole crumb in one face, or accept the mono for identifiers and nudge its size up to optically match.

findings.location: provenance banner card, y 136-423, x 504-1415 (right two-fifths of the card, beside the producer paragraph)
findings.finding: The banner is the only prose container rendered at the full 911 px column width while its text measure is capped around 630 px: every line ends by x=1136 inside a box whose inner edge is x=1390, so ~280 px — a third of the widest, tallest card on the page — is empty white, against 26 px of left padding. Every other prose container here (Not observable card, the ABI note, the three empty-state cards) solves the same problem the opposite way, by capping the box itself at 700 px so the text fills it. Two strategies for one problem, and the ragged one is on the element whose job is to be believed. Cap the banner box at the same 700 px as the other cards, or drop the internal measure cap and let the paragraph use the box it was given.

findings.location: vertical rhythm between sections — rules at y=1007, 1345, 1684, 2299 versus the unruled Internal calls (heading y=1894) and State changes (heading y=2074)
findings.finding: Six peer sections get two different separations. Overview, Decoded input, Events and Raw each open with a full-width hairline and ~131 px of clear space above the heading (~100 px card-to-rule plus 31 px rule-to-heading). Internal calls and State changes open with 55 px and no rule. Because each heading sits 32 px above its own card, the proximity ratio through that stretch is 55:32 — 1.7:1 — where the ruled sections run about 8:1, so the two trace-derived sections read as sub-blocks of Events rather than its peers. Either give all six the same rule and lead-in, or, if Events/Internal calls/State changes are meant to be one group, make the intra-group gap unambiguously tighter than the heading-to-card gap it competes with.

findings.location: gap between each section heading and its first content block — Overview y=1054-1070 versus Events y=1731-1763
findings.finding: One structural relationship is spaced at two values. A heading followed by a table or the Raw block clears 15-16 px (Overview 1054->1070, Decoded input 1393->1408, Raw ~2347->2362); a heading followed by a card clears 32 px (Events 1731->1763, Internal calls 1910->1942, State changes ~2090->2122). Both values are on the scale, but the doubling tracks the child element's type rather than any difference in relationship, so the page's section openings do not repeat. Set one heading-to-content value and let the card's own border, not its margin, carry the difference.

findings.location: Overview table, fourth row (COST · TRANSACTIONFEE), y 1183-1246
findings.finding: The 161 px label column cannot hold this label on one line, so it breaks after `COST ·` and the row becomes 63 px tall against 37, 38 and 38 px for BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY — the table's row rhythm breaks on its last row. The value is top-aligned to the label's first line (value band 1197-1209 in a row whose centre is 1214), so it also sits ~11 px above the row centre and off the vertical rhythm of the three values above it. Widening the label column is not free here — the value already runs to x=1358 inside a 1390 px inner edge — so the fix is a shorter display label or a shorter value, after which the row returns to the 38 px pitch.

findings.location: right edge of the content column between the ABI note (y=1507) and the Raw section rule (y=2299)
findings.finding: For roughly 790 px of page height the only things reaching the column's right edge at x=1415 are two hairline rules; all four cards in that stretch stop at x=1203, so 212 px of the declared column stays empty and each section reads as unfinished on the right while a thin line juts past it. The full width is legitimately used higher up (both tables, the Raw block), so the column itself is not wrong — but the rules should not be the widest thing in a section. Either inset the rules to the width of the content they head, or give the empty-state cards the full column width.

findings.location: state card, `Not observable` badge, versus the `Succeeded` badge beside the hash and the `Finalized` badge in the Overview table
findings.finding: Colour emphasis runs opposite to information weight. The page's headline state is its lowest-emphasis chip — white fill, #c8c8c8 hairline, #565656 text — while three routine facts carry saturated green (#dcfce7 fill, #16a34a border, #166534 text). A reader scanning by colour sees three affirmative chips and misses the one statement the page exists to make. Give the not-observable state its own strong-neutral tone — a filled neutral at the green chips' saturation weight, e.g. a #e4e4e4 fill with a #767676 border and #242424 text — so it is the most emphatic chip on the page without borrowing an alarm hue.

findings.location: Overview table, CANONICAL row versus FINALITY row
findings.finding: Green is applied to affirmative values inconsistently within one grid. `Finalized` is a green pill and `Yes` — one row above, equally affirmative — is a neutral #f3f3f3 pill with identical border and text colours. Nothing on the page states which affirmative facts earn chromatic reinforcement, so green reads as decoration rather than a role. Pick one rule: either every affirmative enum value is green, or green is reserved for a named axis (consensus state only) and canonicality plus outcome revert to neutral.

findings.location: Raw (chain-native) panel, versus the Events / Internal calls / State changes notes and the Overview table
findings.finding: Three container surface treatments coexist with no mapping to what they hold: shadowed white (provenance banner, state card, Overview and Decoded input tables), flat white with a #a2a2a2 hairline and no shadow (the four prose notes), and outline-only whose fill is #ececeb — pixel-identical to the page canvas — for the Raw JSON panel. The Raw panel therefore has zero fill contrast against the page and reads as a stray outline rather than a surface. Either give it the flat-white fill the other panels use, or, if a recessed code well is intended, take it at least two steps below canvas (around #e0e0df) so the recess is visible and define which containers are raised and which are recessed.

findings.location: Overview and Decoded input tables, label column; and the resolver field in the fixed nav
findings.finding: The label-column fill is #dddddd, which is darker than the page canvas #ececeb, so a sub-cell inside an elevated white card sits below the un-elevated page background and the elevation ramp is not monotonic. The same #dddddd is also the nav resolver input's fill, giving one surface token two jobs — table label cell and text input. Lighten the label cell to sit between canvas and card (around #f3f3f3, the token the `Yes` pill already uses) and keep #dddddd for input fills only.

findings.location: footer provenance strip, the heart in `Built with <heart> by`; and the Chains / About links in the fixed nav
findings.finding: The accent indigo #4f46e5 carries the link role everywhere in content — breadcrumb, the `67113:0` block link, all four footer links — but has exceptions in both directions: the heart glyph is the same #4f46e5 while being non-interactive, and the nav's Chains and About links are #484848 with no underline. Decide whether indigo is the link colour, then tint the heart off the accent (a body-text or muted-accent fill) and either promote the nav links to the link colour or record chrome-grey as a deliberate nav treatment.

findings.location: state card, second paragraph (the getTxByHash pruning reason); and the provenance banner body copy
findings.finding: The two passages the expectation block grades as content sit at the page's lowest content emphasis. Inside the state card the generic lead sentence is #242424 while the published pruning reason below it is #484848, demoting the substantive text under the boilerplate; the banner's producer sentences are also #484848, the same token as the footer's fine print. Contrast is fine (9.2:1), but the emphasis ladder argues against the content. Set the published reason and the banner body at #242424 and reserve #484848 for genuinely secondary copy.

findings.location: Overview table, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row, value cell
findings.finding: The fee is printed as the raw zero-padded 32-byte word: 50 leading zeros fill roughly 78% of the cell's width before the 15 significant digits appear, so the row's information-per-pixel is near zero and the magnitude is unreadable at a glance. Render the quantity as a grouped decimal with the unit (e.g. "105,...,912 mana (FeeJuice)"), or at minimum strip the leading zeros and keep the full padded word behind a copy/title affordance.

findings.location: Overview table, label column, COST · TRANSACTIONFEE row
findings.finding: The label is the adapter's camelCase field name uppercased, so it renders as the unbroken 14-character token TRANSACTIONFEE with no word boundary — measurably slower to parse than the three single-word labels above it — and it is the only label that wraps, making this row twice the height of BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY while its value occupies one line. Split the field name into words at capitals ("Transaction fee") before display so the label column can hold every label on one line at this width.

findings.location: whole page at the 1920px viewport — single content column from x≈505 to x≈1418
findings.finding: The wide breakpoint is not used: one ~910px column sits centred with ~500px of empty canvas on each side while the page runs 2872px tall, and the 1080px fold falls on the top border of the Overview table, so a reader on this viewport sees the provenance banner, the hash and the reason but not a single metadata value — the half of §7.0 that is explicitly not a consolation prize is entirely below the fold. Pair Overview with Decoded input as two columns at this breakpoint (both hold short values in a half-width cell) to lift the metadata above the fold and cut roughly a screen of scroll.

findings.location: Events, Internal calls and State changes sections, y≈1690–2230
findings.finding: Three heading-plus-card pairs, each two lines of near-identical boilerplate, consume about 780px of vertical space — three quarters of a viewport — to convey one fact the reason card has already stated. At 910px of column each card's text ends well short of its right edge. Set the three as a 3-up row of equal-height cards at the wide breakpoint, or keep the headings stacked and reduce the cards to a single line each, so the section list stays scannable as structure rather than reading as three paragraphs.

findings.location: provenance banner, body paragraph — text wraps at x≈1139 inside a card whose right edge is x≈1418
findings.finding: The banner's prose is measure-capped about 30% narrower than the card that holds it, leaving an empty gutter down all nine lines and costing roughly two extra lines of height at the very top of the fold. Either narrow the card to its text measure or let the paragraph use the card's width, so the densest text block on the page does not spend fold height on a gutter.

findings.location: Decoded input section, SELECTOR and RAW rows plus the ABI note card, y≈1370–1580
findings.finding: A two-row table and a full note card — about 210px — are spent on two null values, and the RAW value renders as the bare string "0x", which reads like a truncated hash rather than "no calldata"; the note beneath then says parameters "are shown as raw bytes" when none are shown. Collapse the section to one line stating there is no calldata for this transaction, keeping the ABI sentence only where a selector actually exists.

findings.location: Decoded input section — the note card beneath the SELECTOR/RAW table, approx. x 504-1202, y 1512-1584 in the 1920x2872 image
findings.finding: The note reads "This selector is not in any ABI BlockTracer holds, so the parameters are shown as raw bytes. Supplying an ABI decodes them." but the table directly above it renders SELECTOR as an em dash (correctly: no selector exists) and RAW as an empty `0x`. No raw bytes are shown, there is no selector to miss in an ABI, and supplying an ABI would decode nothing. This is generic unknown-selector copy firing on an absent-payload state, so one state is presented as a different state and a remedy is offered that cannot succeed. On the one page in the product whose entire thesis is "a permanent answer rather than a failed fetch", a sentence telling the reader an action on their part would produce more data contradicts the page's central claim in its own voice. Gate the note on an actual unknown-selector value, and when the payload is empty say so — "this transaction publishes no calldata" — in the value slot instead of a fallback prefix plus an inapplicable explanation.

findings.location: Overview table, fourth row, label cell — `COST · TRANSACTIONFEE`, approx. x 504-668, y 1192-1240
findings.finding: The label's second half is the adapter's raw camelCase field name `transactionFee`, uppercased by the label style into the unreadable single run `TRANSACTIONFEE`, which also forces this row's label to wrap to two lines while BLOCK, CANONICAL and FINALITY sit on one. The pattern the row belongs to is `COST · <unit>` — the synthetic chain fills that slot with a tidy `MANA`. Here an internal identifier from the ingestion layer has reached a marketing-grade surface, and it is the only label on the page that is not product vocabulary; a reader learns the shape of our adapter rather than the name of the thing they are paying. The value cell compounds it: a 44-zero-padded 32-byte hex string followed by `mana (FeeJuice)`, i.e. the wire encoding plus two competing unit names. Map the field to the chain's own display unit (`MANA`) in the label and render the amount as a decimal quantity in that unit.

findings.location: Provenance banner, lines 5-6 ("settled 20 transaction(s)", "7 block(s) below the window") and the Not observable card, line 4 ("6 block(s) below it")
findings.finding: The parenthesised plural stub `(s)` appears three times across the page's two most important pieces of copy — the banner that establishes this data is real, and the reason that establishes the trace can never exist. It is an unmistakable engineering tell: no shipped web surface in the 2026 direction writes "20 transaction(s)". It lands hardest here because these are precisely the two sentences the product asks the reader to believe, and a template artefact in them makes them read as machine output rather than as a statement someone stands behind. Pluralise properly in the producer's string formatting ("20 transactions", "7 blocks", "6 blocks"), handling the singular case rather than deferring it to the reader.

findings.location: Provenance banner, sentences 2-3 — "NO TRANSACTION INSIDE IT WAS REPLAYABLE, so this chain publishes real blocks and real transactions and no traces. That is what the capture found, not a failure to record."
findings.finding: One clause is set in full capitals inside eight lines of otherwise sentence-case prose, and it is immediately followed by a denial ("not a failure to record"). The banner is the affirmative-tone element on the page — its job is to state calmly that this data is real — and shouting plus self-defence gives it the voice of an incident notice, which is the opposite of the register the page needs and the opposite of what the rest of the page achieves. The denial is also redundant: the Not observable card twenty lines below already carries the spec-mandated "a permanent answer rather than a failed fetch", so the page defends itself twice before it has finished explaining itself once. Drop the capitals to sentence case and let the fact carry its own weight; if emphasis is wanted, use the type system's weight, not caps lock.

findings.location: Provenance banner, line 7 — "Catching one needs a follower that watches the tip continuously rather than a single scan."
findings.finding: This sentence is addressed to whoever maintains the capture tooling, not to someone looking up a transaction: it is a roadmap note about our own ingestion method sitting in the element whose job is to describe the chain. Beyond the audience mismatch it works against the page's required framing. The transaction-level reason correctly locates the limitation in the chain's retention (getTxByHash prunes at the finalized tip), but this line tells the reader that a differently-built capture would have caught replayable transactions — so a reader assembling the two accounts concludes the shortfall is ours after all, on the page whose brief explicitly requires that nothing here reads as our failure. It stops short of a Must-not-show violation because it is scoped to the 400-block enumeration rather than to this transaction, but it is the one sentence pulling against the rest. Move the capture-methodology note to the chain page or an operations log and leave the banner describing what the network published.

findings.location: Events section, empty-state card (approx. y 1780-1850) read against the identically-styled Internal calls and State changes cards below it
findings.finding: Three visually identical empty-state cards run down the page, but two speak in the permanent tense ("empty permanently, not yet") and the middle one speaks in the pending tense ("They appear here once this chain's receipts are published"). The information is defensible — receipts are not a trace and could genuinely arrive — but the shared card treatment invites the reader to take the three as one message, and one forward-looking promise in that set softens the permanence the page is built to communicate. Either differentiate the pending card visually from the permanent ones, or make the events copy state the same kind of fact the others do — what this chain publishes today, rather than what it might publish later.

resolutions.evidence: client/src/pages/tx.nim: the H1 called truncHash(v.hash, lead=10, tail=8) while the breadcrumb called truncHash(v.hash) with its 6/4 defaults, so ONE hash appeared at three lengths inside 130 vertical pixels. The H1 now uses the same defaults, so the page has exactly two forms — one truncation rule and the full value. MEASURED on the rebuilt page: the distinct 0x-prefixed string lengths are 11 (truncated), 42 (full), 10 (the selector) and 2 ('0x'), i.e. one truncation length, not three.

client/src/components/styles.nim adds `.badge.lg` at --bt-type-body-sm-size with --bt-space-2xs/--bt-space-sm padding, and client/src/pages/tx.nim renders the hero outcome with it. The hero status badge moves from the 12px label rung to the 14px body rung beside the 32px H1, so the second most important fact on a page about reverted transactions is no longer the smallest type in the hero.

client/src/pages/tx.nim: the cost cell was `c.used & " / " & c.limit & " " & c.unit` in one .identifier span with no space before the token parenthetical. The figures keep the identifier treatment; the unit and the token drop to .muted, and the space is restored — `42000 / 100000` mono, then ` mana (FeeJuice)` at the secondary level. The digits are the scannable part again. Thousands grouping is NOT addressed: the values arrive as strings from the data contract and inserting separators would be the view computing a presentation of a chain-native quantity, which Data-Contract.md forbids the view from doing. Left for VD.4 with the fee rows.

client/src/components/styles.nim: `.sec-title` margin-bottom moved from --bt-rhythm-stack (24px) to --bt-space-xs (8px) while `.sec-title.next` keeps padding-top: --bt-rhythm-stack (24px) below its rule. MEASURED on the rebuilt page, gap above / gap below for the six headings: 100/8, 100/8, 100/24, 48/24, 48/24, 100/8. Every heading is now 3x-4x closer to the content it labels than to the boundary above it, so proximity binds each heading downwards.

client/src/components/styles.nim adds `.sec-title.sibling` at --bt-rhythm-group (48px) with no rule, and client/src/pages/tx.nim applies it to Internal calls and State changes — three one-sentence sibling sections are separated by the GROUP step and the group as a whole by the SECTION step, which is what the four rhythm roles exist to express. MEASURED: the section gaps are now 100/100/100/48/48/100px rather than six identical 100px aprons, and the page is 2583px tall against 2785px before.

client/src/components/styles.nim: `.debugcard .note.spec` gains max-width:none. The rule was asymmetric (25px left, 65px right) because it belonged to a paragraph capped at --bt-measure-prose sitting inside a card capped at --bt-layout-prose — two different measures, one nested in the other. The rule now spans the card's content box, and the card's own width is the measure.

client/src/components/styles.nim: every container now carries the SAME hairline in --bt-border-default — the trace card (was --bt-border-strong, read as borderless beside its overlay shadow), the code block (was --bt-border-subtle plus a fill) and the callouts (which also lose their thick left spine). Containers are ranked by ONE axis, elevation: the trace card is the only panel carrying --bt-elevation-overlay, the data panels carry --bt-elevation-raised, the callouts carry none. One idiom, one ranking.

client/src/pages/tx.nim renders Canonical with the neutral badge role instead of the success role — canonicality is a registry fact, not an execution outcome — so green means execution status and only that. client/src/viewutil.nim returns the information role for taOnDemand, so the trace-coverage state the page turns on carries a hue again. The two axes stay distinguishable by SHAPE as well as colour: a status badge is a filled rectangle, a coverage chip is an outlined pill with a leading dot (.badge.coverage).

The four emphasis levels were not the problem — the ROLE ASSIGNMENT was: --bt-text-muted (#484848) carried breadcrumb, eyebrow, grid labels, every explanatory panel and the footer at once. client/src/components/styles.nim spreads them: chrome (breadcrumb, eyebrow, footer) drops to --bt-text-subtle, labels stay --bt-text-muted, and explanatory PROSE — which is content, not chrome — rises to --bt-text-default. Three levels now do three jobs. Widening the ladder further is not available in pure greys: on the sunken surface (#f3f3f3) only neutral.450 and darker clear 4.5:1, which is why the rungs are close; VD.10 owns the palette audit.

client/src/components/styles.nim: the section rules move from --bt-border-subtle (#c8c8c8, 1.86:1 on white) to --bt-border-default (#a2a2a2, 2.60:1). It is an improvement, not conformance: WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 floor applies to UI components and meaningful graphics, and a decorative section rule is neither — the section boundary is also carried by a 100px gap and a heading. A 3:1 rule grid would read as a spreadsheet in a marketing-grade register. Recorded here rather than exempted; VD.10 re-runs the audit over the final palette.

Same change as tx-detail/wide/light/L2/5, which L4 reached independently from the density lens: `.sec-title.sibling` at --bt-rhythm-group for the three trace-derived sections. Two reviewers with different lenses measured the same defect, which is the signal the five-lens design exists to produce.

resolutions.reason: P3. The two widths are a decision, not raggedness: data panels take the column (--bt-layout-container), prose panels take one shared prose width (--bt-layout-prose). This is a recorded TENSION rather than an agreement — L2 asked twice for the trace panel to be narrowed to its content (round 3) and then for one right edge (round 5), and those cannot both hold. The narrowing won because a 910px box around a 150px button and two sentences made the container outweigh the control it holds. What WAS fixed is the accidental part: the two prose panels previously sat at different widths because --bt-measure-prose is in `ch` and they were set at different font sizes; both now use one px token, so the page has two widths rather than three.

P3. The 92px vs 100px difference is margin collapsing between the trace card's box and the following section's margin-top, not a second spacing step: both are --bt-rhythm-section. Correcting it would mean giving one boundary a hand-written offset, which is the class of ad-hoc margin the rhythm roles exist to eliminate. Read and declined.

P3, and a genuine conflict between two readings from the same lens two rounds apart. Round 2's L2 reported that the badge's TEXT started 10px right of the other values and asked for text alignment; round 5's L2 reports that the badge's BOX starts 9px left of the other values and asks for box alignment.
